Refs KS-1855

Linear ticket: https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1855

**BLUF:** TIER 1 (it changes which routes the gateway answers itself, on a verification door). This is HALF TWO of Kam's c-split of this ticket (card `secuura-ks1855-gateway-standin-routes-1110`, ruling c: "gate certification verify behind the test flag until the rewire lands"). In `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts`, `POST /api/certifications/:id/verify` was registered with no flag or environment gate of its own and answered every request from a gateway stand-in, with no auth handler. A new `certificationVerifyStandInOn` gate lets the stand-in answer only when `NODE_ENV` is not `production` AND `ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS` is `true`; otherwise `next('route')` hands the request on, untouched, to the proxy mount for `/api/certifications`, which forwards to originate's own verify route. Eight added lines and one removed in the product file (develop `ae5b615f4cc0`) plus 24 added lines in two EXISTING test files; no new file. **Half one (the audit-log and verification-queue stand-ins in `routes/admin.ts`, O125-P3) is NOT in this PR, and the ticket stays open.**

## What changes
- **Product, `verification.ts` (+8 -1):** the `certificationVerifyStandInOn` gate (a `RequestHandler`, already imported at line 17) with a why-and-ticket comment, placed before `mockBodyParser` on the route at line 378. The gate runs first on purpose: `mockBodyParser` would consume the request body that the proxy needs.
- **Test, `ks1628-gateway-documents-verify-is-removed.test.ts` (+20):** its existing G2 control (the certifications twin still answers) now stubs the flag on, and two new cells read the route as unanswered by the router (a 404 with no handler): H1 with the flag unset, H2 with the flag `true` but `NODE_ENV` `production`.
- **Test, `ks815-verification-router-guards-its-own-body.test.ts` (+4):** a `beforeAll` and `afterAll` stub of the flag around its three verify-route cells (NUL, nested NUL, clean body), which measure the BODY guard on this route and so need it to answer.
- **Behaviour change, in plain words (flag unset, the default):** the gateway stops answering this route. The request goes on to the proxy mount at `routes/proxy.ts` lines 663 to 668 (`authenticateToken(false)`, `attachScopes`, `requireScope('certifications:read', 'certifications:write')`), which forwards it to originate's own `POST /api/certifications/:id/verify` (`services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts` line 1244). The verification router is mounted at `index.ts` line 937 and the proxy routes at line 1143, so a request the gate hands on reaches the proxy; `/api/certifications` is on the gateway's `proxyPaths` list (line 390). **What an unauthenticated caller gets from that chain was NOT measured by me**; the stand-in had no auth handler at all (recorded in a comment of the ks815 test).
- **Ruling:** the behaviour change is Kam's ruling (c) on the card above. The flag, `ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS` (the gate the mock wallet routes already use in `index.ts`), is the o125 operator's choice as recorded in the 2026-11-10 daily note.
- **Left alone on purpose:** the comment near `verification.ts` lines 446 to 447 says the stand-in "implements a test-only flow that originate doesn't expose". Originate does expose this route (line 1244 above), so that comment is stale; per the o125 operator's note it is LEFT and is not this PR's change.

## Consumers the gate must weigh (measured at develop `ae5b615f4cc0`; nothing of theirs is edited)
- The string `/api/certifications/` sits in **136 files** (docs, SDKs, connectors, tests); **55** of them are test or script paths. The verify route by id is called from **3 test files at 5 call sites**: `ks1628` (1) and `ks815` (3), both edited here, and **`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/verifier-exhaustive.prelaunch.spec.ts` line 298** (Peter's end-to-end spec).
- That spec sets no `ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS` (its only lines naming certifications or mock are 150 and 298), and `docker-compose.yml` line 523 defaults the flag to false (`${ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS:-false}`), so **in a default stack this PR changes that call's answer from the stand-in's to originate's.** Whether his own env file sets the flag is NOT measured. I edited nothing of his spec.
- Non-test callers named: `frontend/issuer/src/services/api.ts` line 481 and `sdk/javascript/src/modules/certifications.ts` line 129. `sdk/python` and four connectors (euro-office, flutter, libreoffice, nextcloud) also use the prefix; which of them call verify was NOT measured.
- Stacks: `docker-compose.production.yml` line 85 sets the flag to false. The demo (UAT) stack's value was NOT measured by me.
- **Provenance of the patch:** a held local-model queue patch, applied unmodified. Canonical patch: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/2_Project_Files/local-model/runs/spark_secuura_2026-11-10_ks_1855_o125_p4_gateway_certification_verify_stand_in_answers_only_when_mock_endpoints_are_on/out.md.checker/patch.diff`. Its added (32) and removed (1) lines are byte-identical to the held ready file's, the applied tree's changed lines per file equal the patch's, and git applied it with NO offset (every hunk exact). The Spark checker's own line, measured by it at its tip `d0b4825cc244` and not at this develop: `PASS A2 diff applies at the tip (strict git apply --check, every section, hunk headers consistent)`; its red-first (2 failed of 22) and green (22 of 22) figures at that tip match mine below.
- **Open PRs:** none touches `verification.ts`, the two test files or `KS-1855` (census at the push, with controls).

## Red, green (measured on this tree's bytes)
- The two edited test files run together over develop's UNCHANGED product: 2 failed (H1, H2) and 20 passed of 22. With this change: 22 of 22.
- **Whole `services/api-gateway` suite, run 3 times before and 3 times after (interleaved pairs, before then after, so load drift hits both sides alike; load1 14.7 to 18.0 while other jobs ran):** before the change 170 files and 1,904 tests, exit status 0 in 3 of 3 runs; after the change 170 files and 1,906 tests (the two new cells), exit status 0 in 3 of 3. No test failed in any of the six runs.
- `tsc --noEmit` on the service's own `tsconfig.json`: rc 0, no diagnostics (after the change). With the test files in the program (a scratch config; a planted-error control fires): rc 2 on 25 diagnostic lines that all sit in six other test files (`csrf`, `ks1165`, `ks1374`, `ks1464`, `ks695`, `rateLimitEnforce`), none in a changed file.
- eslint on the three changed files (absolute paths, the repo's root flat config): 0 errors, 0 warnings.

## Test plan / Test Evidence
- **Touched:** `services/api-gateway` only: one product file and two existing test files. No fragment pair added: the docs-fragments check passes without one (measured).
- **Ran** (Node v26.8.1, not the Node 24 LTS line; one Apple Silicon host; vitest through `npm test -- run` in the package): the two edited test files red and green; the whole suite 3 times before and 3 times after as above; `tsc --noEmit` plain and with tests as above; eslint as above; `docs-fragments.mjs check`: OK.
- **NOT run:** any other service's suite; the four platform suites (Schemathesis, Akto, Playwright, k6); Docker or the compose stack; a real gateway and originate pair (the fall-through to originate is read from source, not exercised); Peter's end-to-end spec and every other consumer call; Node 24. The pre-merge acknowledgement boxes for Schemathesis and Akto are therefore NOT ticked.
- **Migrations + config:** none in the PR. A stack that still relies on the stand-in must now set `ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS=true` on the gateway (never in production: `production-guard.ts` in `packages/shared` line 31 lists it among the mock flags; I did not re-read what the guard does with it).
- **Pre-push hook:**

```
PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.
  legs 3 4 8 — local stack not up; you can clear this by starting it.
  This is NOT a pass. Do not quote it as one — say which legs ran.
```
- Leg 14, verbatim: `shell suites: 127 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (of 127)`

## Before this deploys
Nothing deploys from this PR. The change takes effect only after the api-gateway image is rebuilt and the service redeployed. No migration, schema or secret changes. On deploy, in any stack without `ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS=true`, certification verify requests stop being answered by the gateway and reach originate through the proxy chain described above; check the demo stack's flag before it is redeployed.

## Not claimed
Half one of the ticket (`routes/admin.ts`), the originate to anchoring rewire the stand-in's comments wait for, whether originate's answer suits every caller, or that the ticket is done. This PR selects the certification verify stand-in only.

Refs KS-1197

Linear ticket: https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1197

**BLUF:** TIER 1 (an authorisation rule on document creation: which verification level an authenticated principal is held to). A PARTIAL DEFENCE, not the ticket's fix. In `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts`, `meetsVerificationLevel` read `(userLevel || 'none').toLowerCase()` and `enforceDocumentTypeRules` read `user.verificationLevel || 'none'`; a truthy value that is not a string (a number, an array, an object off a token claim) passed the `||` and threw a TypeError, which the ticket reports as a 500 on `POST /api/documents`. A level that is not a string now ranks as `none`, the lowest authenticated level, exactly as an unrecognised level already does (`KS-1176`): it meets a `none` requirement and nothing above it. Three added lines and two removed in one product file (develop `ae5b615f4cc0`) plus one new test file (102 lines, 13 cells). What this does NOT fix is listed below; the ticket stays open.

## What changes
- **Product, `enforcement.ts` (+3 -2):** both rank reads take the level only when it is a non-empty string (`typeof level === 'string' && level ? level : 'none'`), with a why-and-ticket comment on the first. Hunk 1 is `meetsVerificationLevel` (line 54); hunk 2 is the `userLevel` read in `enforceDocumentTypeRules` (line 153).
- **New cell file, `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1197-a-non-string-verification-level-ranks-as-none.test.ts` (102 lines, 13 cells):** drives `enforceDocumentTypeRules` and `meetsVerificationLevel` directly (not the route over HTTP). K1: a number, an array and an object level meet nothing above `none` (a `standard` type refuses with 403). K2: the 403 text names the level as `NONE`. K3: such a level still meets a `none` requirement. K4 and K5: `meetsVerificationLevel` reads true against `none` and false against `basic`. Controls C1 to C4 pin the known levels and the connector-key level, which must not change.
- **Behaviour change, in plain words:** a principal whose claim is not a string used to hit a TypeError at this rule check. It is now refused with 403 by a type that requires more than `none`, and admitted by a type that requires `none`. That second half is what ranking as `none` means, and it is the treatment an unrecognised level already gets.
- **Provenance of the patch:** the fix shape is a held local-model queue patch, not the ticket's recommendation (validate or coerce the claim once where the principal is built). Canonical patch: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/2_Project_Files/local-model/runs/spark_secuura_2026-10-28_ks_1197_p1/out.md.checker/patch.diff`, applied unmodified. Its added and removed lines are byte-identical to the held ready file's (105 added, 2 removed), the applied tree's changed lines per file equal the patch's, and git applied it with its own offset of 1 line on hunk 2 and nothing else (hunk 1 exact). The Spark checker's own line, measured by it at its tip `1d07ce26ae2f` and not at this develop: `PASS A2 diff applies at the tip (strict git apply --check, every section, hunk headers consistent)`; its red-first (9 failed of 13) and green (13 of 13) figures at that tip match mine below.
- **Open PRs:** none touches `enforcement.ts`, the new test path or `KS-1197` (census at the push, with controls).

## What this PR does NOT fix
1. **Validation where the principal is built (`middleware/auth.ts`).** A non-string claim still enters the request as it did; this PR only makes the two rank checks tolerate it.
2. **The `__proto__` path.** The ticket's 2026-10-12 comment describes a level that can be set through `routes/users.ts` (about lines 622 to 647) and read back through `userRepo.ts` `mapDbVerificationLevel`. Unchanged here, and not re-measured by me.
3. **The verify-handler hang the ticket names.** `meetsVerificationLevel` is NOT that handler's call. Measured at develop `ae5b615f4cc0`: the function has one product caller, `enforceDocumentTypeRules` (`enforcement.ts` line 154), which `routes/verification.ts` calls at line 932 inside `router.post('/api/documents', ...)` (registered at line 739, the document-create route); the other uses are two test files. The step-approval check at `routes/verification.ts` lines 544 to 566 (inside the workflow-instances approve route, registered at line 524) uses neither function. Any hang there is untouched by this PR.

## Red, green (measured on this tree's bytes)
- The new cell file alone, against develop's unchanged product: 9 failed (K1 to K5 over a number, an array and an object) and 4 passed (C1 to C4). With this change: 13 of 13.
- **Whole `services/api-gateway` suite, run 3 times before and 3 times after (interleaved pairs, before then after, so load drift hits both sides alike; load1 3.4 to 19.4 while other jobs ran):** before the change 170 files and 1,904 tests, exit status 0 in 3 of 3 runs; after the change 171 files and 1,917 tests (the 13 new cells), exit status 0 in 3 of 3. No test failed in any of the six runs.
- `tsc --noEmit` on the service's own `tsconfig.json`: rc 0, no diagnostics (after the change). With the test files in the program (a scratch config; a planted-error control fires): rc 2 on 25 diagnostic lines that all sit in six other test files (`csrf`, `ks1165`, `ks1374`, `ks1464`, `ks695`, `rateLimitEnforce`), none in either changed file.
- eslint on the two changed files (absolute paths, the repo's root flat config): 0 errors and 1 warning, `no-useless-assignment` at line 62 of the new test (`let message = 'THREW'` is overwritten in both branches). Left as the held patch has it: the patch is applied unmodified.

## Test plan / Test Evidence
- **Touched:** `services/api-gateway` only: one product file and one new test file. No fragment pair added: the docs-fragments check passes without one (measured).
- **Ran** (Node v26.8.1, not the Node 24 LTS line; one Apple Silicon host; vitest through `npm test -- run` in the package): the new cell file red and green; the whole suite 3 times before and 3 times after as above; `tsc --noEmit` plain and with tests as above; eslint as above; `docs-fragments.mjs check`: OK.
- **NOT run:** any other service's suite; the four platform suites (Schemathesis, Akto, Playwright, k6); Docker or the compose stack; a real service start; the `POST /api/documents` route over HTTP; Node 24. The pre-merge acknowledgement boxes for Schemathesis and Akto are therefore NOT ticked.
- **Migrations + config:** none.
- **Pre-push hook:**

```
PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.
  legs 3 4 8 — local stack not up; you can clear this by starting it.
  This is NOT a pass. Do not quote it as one — say which legs ran.

- Leg 14, verbatim: `shell suites: 127 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (of 127)`

Nothing deploys from this PR. The change takes effect only after the api-gateway image is rebuilt and the service redeployed; no migration, config or secret changes, and no API or schema change. On deploy, a request whose principal carries a non-string verification level stops hitting a TypeError at this rule and is ruled on as level `none` (403 above `none`, admitted at `none`).

That the ticket's forgeable-claim path or its verify-handler hang is addressed (it is not), validation at the principal, or any other field. The same `.toLowerCase()` pattern on a `role` value sits at `routes/verification.ts` line 551 (the step-approval check); this PR does not touch it and I did not measure whether a non-string role can reach it. Refs KS-1776

Linear ticket: https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1776

**BLUF:** Tier 2. Importing `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` arms a module-scope 2000 ms `setTimeout` that calls `userRepo.seedDemoUsers(hashPassword).catch(...)`. The `.catch` handled a rejection only; a SYNCHRONOUS throw from the call (a repository mock that lacks the export, a repository that is not ready) escaped the timer as an uncaught exception, which the test runner pins on whichever test is running. The call now sits in a `try/catch` and both the throw and the rejection go to one shared `logSeedFailure`, which writes the same `Failed to seed demo users` line as before. Ten added lines and three removed in `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` (develop `1dd6299bccd6`) plus one new test file. No auth decision, token, credential, database write or response changes; the seed itself is unchanged.

## What changes
- **Product, `routes/auth.ts` (+10 -3):** a `logSeedFailure` helper with a why-and-ticket comment, and the timer's call wrapped in `try { ... .catch(logSeedFailure) } catch (err) { logSeedFailure(err) }`. The timer, its 2000 ms delay and the log message are unchanged.

Refs KS-1913

Linear ticket: https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1913

**BLUF:** Tier 2. The platform audit log page colours six known actions and shows any other in a muted fallback style. Deleting a tenant now writes `tenant_archived` (or `tenant_archive_failed` on failure) instead of `tenant_deleted`, so both new actions rendered muted where `tenant_deleted` was red, and a failed archive looked like routine noise. `tenant_archived` now gets an orange badge and `tenant_archive_failed` the same red classes as `tenant_deleted`. Three added lines in `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/admin/src/pages/platform/PlatformAuditLog.tsx` (develop `410feda1a85e`) plus one new test file. No new hue: orange-500 is already used in `components/Layout.tsx` (lines 325 and 335); the class combination follows the neighbouring badges.

- **Product, `PlatformAuditLog.tsx` (+3 -0):** two entries in the `actionStyles` map and one why-and-ticket comment line above them. The existing entries, the fallback style and the page logic are unchanged.
- **New cell file, `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/admin/src/__tests__/ks1913-platform-audit-log-archive-actions-are-styled.test.tsx` (56 lines, 3 cells):** renders the real page with the api module replaced. ## Refs KS-1988 (and `KS-2075`): the migration readiness probe parses a URL with no port or host, and observability down survives an absent redis container

**TIER 1: product bytes change; tier 1 (Wednesday's ruling, model-routing rule 4: Spark edits inside auth, security, audit and hook files); the gate may raise it.** Two shell scripts change by three lines in all: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh` (+2 -2) and `observability/scripts/observability.sh` (+1 -1), with two new bash tests. Two held Spark passes, raised as ONE pull request on disjoint files. Merge to develop only.

Linear: https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1988 and `https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-2075`

## Summary

- **`KS-1988`, `run-migrations.sh`.** The readiness probe cut the host and the port out of `DATABASE_URL` with two `sed -E` commands that assume `USER:PASS@HOST:PORT/DB`. When the URL does not match (no port, or no host as with a socket-directory URL), `sed` without `-n` prints the whole line unchanged, so `pg_isready` was handed the whole URL as host and port and the runner exited 2 after its 60 s. Both commands now use `sed -nE ... p`, so an unmatched URL gives an EMPTY host or port, and the existing line `PG_PORT=${PG_PORT:-5432}` supplies the default port. Behaviour change to read: an empty host reaches `pg_isready` as `-h ""` (its default, the local socket), so a socket-style URL can now become ready where it used to time out.
- **`KS-2075`, `observability.sh`.** `_redis_pw="$(resolve_redis_password)"` sits at file scope under `set -euo pipefail`, so when the platform's redis container is absent the failing `docker inspect` ends the script before the `down)` branch is reached. It becomes `$(resolve_redis_password || true)`. **Scope, stated plainly: the guard is at file scope, so it applies to EVERY action, not only `down`: with the container absent, every action now proceeds with the password unset instead of exiting 1 at the lookup. Only `down` is pinned by the new cell; what `start`, `status` and `logs` do in that state is NOT measured.**
- **The tests, fakes only.** Each new bash test puts stubs on a private `PATH` (a recording `pg_isready` and a `psql` for the first, a recording `docker` for the second): no database, no Docker, no network, and the only URLs are placeholders (`u:pw`). The first has three cells (a URL with host and port is split correctly; a URL with no port probes port 5432; a URL with no host probes an empty host on 5432); the second has two (a present container; an absent container, where `down` must exit 0 and run `docker compose ... down` once).
- **What it does NOT do.** It does not change what the runner or the stack does for any URL or state the cells do not cover, and it does not close either ticket: this pull request says `Refs` and both stay open.
- **Held patches** (Spark passes, operator 127 for `KS-1988`, 4,131 B canonical, sha256 prefix `9c9fcffdd7c2d9b1`; operator 128 for `KS-2075`, 3,538 B canonical, sha256 prefix `5985955cf7124904`): each READY's fence equals its canonical patch. Applied strictly at develop `d0e58f55c861`: BOTH ways, whole and per section (the section files differ from the canonical patch by exactly two header lines on each new test file, `diff --git` and `new file mode 100644`; `git apply --check -p1` rc 0 for each of the four sections, for each canonical patch and for the two together; a doctored copy read rc 1). The tree was built from the canonical patches. Nothing in them was changed by Seat R 102nd.

## Test plan / Test Evidence

**Touched:** four files, numstat equal to the held patches': `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh` (2 added 2 removed), `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/run_migrations_readiness_probe_parses_the_url.test.sh` (new, 67 added), `observability/scripts/observability.sh` (1 added 1 removed) and `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/observability_down_survives_an_absent_redis_container.test.sh` (new, 65 added). Base is develop `d0e58f55c861`. The census before the push (GraphQL, all pages, 93 open pull requests, 400 file rows) read no open pull request on any of the four paths; the controls passed (PR 2125's api-gateway file hit exactly PR 2125, the newest open PR's first file hit exactly that PR, an absent path hit nothing). **Host and runtime (stated per the repo's test-discipline skill).** Every run below was made on one Apple Silicon Mac (arm64), macOS 27.2.1, with no Docker stack started (these are stub-driven shell tests, so no stack slot applies), under `/bin/bash` GNU bash 3.2.57 and the macOS BSD `sed`. Refs KS-1497 (https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1497). Items 1, 3, 5 and 6 of the ticket, plus the two symlink cells its gate comment names. Items 2 and 4 were delivered earlier. It does not close the ticket.

## What this does

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/prisma-generate.cjs` is developer tooling that stages the schema in `node_modules/.generate`, runs `prisma generate`, removes the directory and checks the client. Four changes, all in that script and its suite:

- **Item 1, signals.** A SIGINT or SIGTERM used to kill the script at once: the `finally` never ran, `node_modules/.generate` stayed behind, and a SIGTERM sent to the script alone left the prisma child running. The script now removes the staging directory, kills the child, and exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM). **Exit codes unchanged (130/143), chosen by Wednesday to keep caller-visible behaviour; the fix is the cleanup and the child kill.**
- **Item 3, a stale client.** "OK" was printed when prisma exited 0 and wrote nothing, if a client from an earlier run was present. The client file's modification time must now be no older than the start of this run (one second of slack for coarse file-system timestamps); otherwise exit 2 naming the file. This is the ticket's own first option; the other (remove the old client first) would leave a developer with no client if prisma then failed. Wednesday-accepted choice.
- **Item 5, the OK line.** It was relative to the current directory and printed `../../..` noise from another one. It is now relative to the service directory (`node_modules/.prisma/client/default.js`). Wednesday-accepted choice.
- **Item 6 and the two symlink cells.** A prisma killed by a signal has no exit status and the script exits 1 for it; that was never pinned, and a gate mutant that returned 0 for it survived. It is pinned now, together with the file-symlink and dangling-symlink shapes the ticket's second comment names.

## Why the prisma run became asynchronous

A signal handler cannot run while a synchronous child (`spawnSync`) blocks Node's event loop. Measured on node v26.8.1, with `sleep` standing in for prisma, a SIGTERM to the script alone, 1 s into a 4 s child:

| shape | what happened |
|---|---|
| no handler (develop) | script exits 143 at once; the child is still running |
| handler over `spawnSync` | the handler never ran; the script waited 3.26 s for the child and exited 0 |
| handler over an async `spawn` | the handler ran at +961 ms, killed the child, the script exited 143, no orphan |

So prisma now runs as an async child, and the status check, the existence and freshness checks and the OK line run in its exit callback. The handlers are installed before the staging directory is created. Messages and the other exit codes (0, 2, prisma's own, no status to 1) are unchanged. The restructure is inside the commissioned fix and was Wednesday's call, made on these three measurements.

## Not covered (as the ticket states, neither is a regression)

The window between the `lstat` check and the `mkdirSync`, and a symlinked `node_modules` above `.generate`. SIGHUP is not handled.

## Test Evidence

**Touched (4 files, 1 commit):** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/prisma-generate.cjs`, `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks1497_prisma_generate_refuses_a_bad_staging_dir.test.sh`, and the flow and cheat fragments `KS-1497-prisma-generate-signals-and-stale-client`. No service source file.

**Ran (at the branch head, cut on develop d0e58f55c861):**
- `ks1497_prisma_generate_refuses_a_bad_staging_dir.test.sh`: the old suite 7 passed, 0 failed on develop; the new suite (22 cells) 14 passed and 8 failed against develop's unmodified script (the staging directory and the child left after SIGTERM and after SIGINT, 4; an old client accepted and no refusal text, 2; `../` in the OK line and not the service-relative line, 2); 22 passed and 0 failed against this branch; the original 7 cells still pass against the new script.
- Pins that pass on develop and after (the exit codes 143 and 130, a prisma killed by a signal exits 1, the two symlink shapes): a mutant turns each red. One CONTROL cell shows an old client is accepted when this run's prisma writes a new one.
- Mutants, one change at a time on a scratch copy (the suite takes the script path from `PRISMA_GENERATE_CJS`, so the script under test was never edited): 8 of 8 turn at least one cell red: develop's script with the synchronous spawn (8 cells), no child kill (2), no staging removal (2), exit 1 in the handler (2), a missing prisma status mapped to 0 (1), `stat` for `lstat` (5), no freshness check (2), the OK line relative to the cwd (2). A planted replacement that matched nothing was refused.
- The originate jest suite that spawns the real script, `ks1305-generate-script-reaches-a-generated-client.test.ts`: 9 passed before and after. No other suite names the script or this suite (`git grep` of the tracked tree and `.github`); the strings this change moved or reworded (the old cwd-relative expression and the old suite header) occur only in the two files edited, and the OK-line prefix and the failure text are unchanged.

**Pre-push hook (unfiltered output kept by the author):** `[pre-push] Blockchain/Dev changes detected → running preflight gate (bypass: --no-verify)` was printed. The closing verdict, verbatim: `PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.` Legs 3, 4 and 8 were skipped (local stack not up); the hook itself says this is NOT a pass. Leg 14 read `shell suites: 126 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (of 126)` (shell suites wall-clock: 711s) and runs this change's suite; leg 16 read `OK — 5 service(s) type-check against their baseline.` (develop's five services; this change does not touch them). Pushed through the one-driver queue and lock; nothing was bypassed.

**NOT run:** a real `prisma generate` (the CLI is a stub and the long run the signal cells interrupt is a stand-in child that records its pid and waits); the four platform suites (Schemathesis, Akto, Playwright, k6), which need a stack this change does not touch; any stack, Docker, database or box; any bash but 3.2.57 (the macOS /bin/bash these suites ran under); node other than v26.8.1 (not the LTS line); another operating system; the cells under heavy machine load (the waits are 10 s to see the child start, 8 s for the script to exit, 3 s for the child to die).

## What this does

`services/originate/tsconfig.json` excludes `src/__tests__` and every `*.test.ts`, so `tsc` over the service never examined a test file: a "0 errors" line over a test-only change could not fail, and no push gate looked at them. ## Summary

- **What the ticket records.** Gate finding G306-2168-1 on the merged PR 2168: the catch of `processExport` called `logger.warn` before it set the constant error text and saved the failed state; `createExport` calls `processExport` with no `await` and no `.catch`; so a logger that throws leaves the failed row unsaved, the stored export `processing`, and an unhandled rejection. The ticket's own suggested fix is the order this PR uses, plus a cell with a throwing logger.
- **What changes (three things the body states plainly).** (1) **The failed row is now saved BEFORE the log line:** `exportResult.error = 'Export failed'` and `await this.dbSaveExport(exportResult)` come first. ## Summary

Tier 1 (security surface), size S, one router file.

**What was wrong.** The five notification routes that read or change a stored row (list, unread count, mark-read, read-all, delete) key only on the caller's user id. The gateway builds that id for an API key as `connector:${meta.connectorId || 'api-key'}` (`middleware/auth.ts`, line 572), so every key with no connector id is the one principal `connector:api-key`, whichever tenant minted it: one tenant's key could list and delete the rows another tenant's key had placed in that inbox. The reach is rows that keys posted to themselves. Verified at source by Wednesday's verifier on 2026-11-10, which found no frontend or service caller of these routes; read in code and run on mocks, not on a live box.

**What changes.** The five routes answer 403 `FORBIDDEN` to a connector principal as their first statement, before any store is read, so the answer is the same for an existing id, an unknown id and an empty inbox. A connector principal is any one of four signals the gateway mints together on a key: a user id starting `connector:`, role `connector`, verification level `api_key`, auth method `api_key`. A person's principal carries none of them. `POST /` is unchanged.

**The ruling.** Wednesday's ruling, by the precedent of Kam's KS 2038 card (the transfer doors); Kam has not ruled on notifications.

**Four statements for the gate to test.**
- **(a) A contract changed in KS 1448's test file, which this PR touches.** The KS 1448 cell C1 read a connector key's row back and expected it. That is the behaviour this change removes, so the C1 row is removed from the table and C1b is added: a key still creates for its own id (201, same user id) and the read-back is pinned as 403 `FORBIDDEN`. The file is outside the four paths this change was first commissioned with; Wednesday approved the edit. Open PR 2149 (KS 2123) also edits this file, at insertions about 40 lines away from mine (merge-tree rc 0, tree `07407095e8ca`; a planted same-line edit conflicts, rc 1).
- **(b) The asymmetry, left as found.** A connector key can still CREATE a row for its own id (201) but can no longer READ it back (403). `POST /` is unchanged because the ticket names five routes; whether create should stay open is not decided here.
- **(c) The residue.** The platform-admin login mints the stored `platform_admins.role` as it is, so a stored role of `connector` would be refused (it fails closed). `transferAccess.ts` (lines 112 to 114) says the docker schema CHECKs that column and the Azure migrate script does not; that is not verified.
- **(d)** Node v26.8.1, **not an LTS line**, on every run below.

**The four-signal predicate, and its grep.** Wednesday confirmed it on one condition: each signal is set only on a key or connector path and never on a person's principal. Result, `git grep` at develop `0115269abd11` with a positive control beside every result: in the gateway's non-test source all four are set in one block of `middleware/auth.ts` (lines 572, 574, 576, 577; `req.user = connectorUser` at 592). Widened to services and packages (non-test): the auth service's connector token (`jwt.ts` 289 to 294, type `connector`, so it cannot pass `verifyAccessToken`), originate `metering.ts:81` (a connector principal promoted from a role header), `connectorOrganisationErasure.ts:335` (an erasure context) and provenance labels in `gdprService.ts` (1497, 1726): all connector or key paths. A grep for the literals held in a named constant found none (its control hit `TEST_TOKEN_PREFIX` at `auth.ts:115`). A person's principal reaches `req.user` at `auth.ts:684` (a verified JWT) or `:634` (a test token, only in development or test with an explicit opt-in). No signal is set for a person by any code path, so none was dropped.

**Behaviour change, plainly.** An API-key caller gets 403 on the five notification routes it used to read and delete through. The verifier found no frontend or service caller of them; whether an outside integration calls them is not measured. Whether any live box holds an admin-minted key is not measured.

**Not changed.** `POST /`; `auth.ts:572` and `jwt.ts:289` (the root fix, a per-key identity, is a separate decision for Kam); anything outside the five routes.

https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1991

## Summary

Applies Kam's card choice a for this ticket ("Fix the registry"), in three parts. It includes the registration half that the ticket KS 1647 describes.

**The defect.** Verify by hash ranks the tenants that hold some bytes by their row in `platform_document_registry` and reads at most 8 (v1 `readCrossTenantOriginals`, v2 `crossTenantRowsByHash`; `crossTenantLookup` takes the earliest). That row's `created_at` was the moment the row was written. When the original holder's row was missing or written late, a later registrant's certification was presented as the original's (QA gate 192, finding G192-F1). That defeats Kam's KS 1561 rule that only the original holder's certification counts.

1. **Registration is awaited and never swallowed.** `POST /api/documents` used to call `registerInPlatformRegistry(...).catch(() => {})` unawaited, over a function that only logged a warning. Now the function rejects on failure, the route awaits it before the event, the anchor and the 201, and a failure is logged at ERROR with the stable code `KS-1991 REGISTRY_WRITE_FAILED` (document id and tenant id only). The create still answers 201 with the body unchanged, because the document row is already committed by one autocommit INSERT and the registry is in another database, so failing the request would leave a saved document never anchored rather than undo anything. An idempotent re-POST of the same `documentUuid` runs the same awaited registration before its 200, so a retry heals a missing row; rows already missing are the backfill's.
2. **The backfill.** New `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/backfill-platform-registry.js` writes the missing registry rows: one per (tenant, hash), the tenant's earliest document, its stored `content_hash` verbatim and its own `created_at`. A row under either hash form (bare or `sha256:`) counts as registered. Erased documents (`documents.metadata @> '{"anonymized": true}'`, written by the GDPR erasure), status `deleted` and an empty hash are left out; revoked documents are registered. Tenants that are not `active` are skipped and listed. Dry run by default; `--apply` writes.
3. **The document's own clock.** `registerInPlatformRegistry` reads back the tenant document row's `created_at` (exact, as text) and writes it as the registry row's `created_at`; on conflict the upsert keeps the EARLIEST (`LEAST`). The backfill writes the same clock. The rank SQL is unchanged.

**The live upsert vs the backfill (two different rules).** The live upsert's `LEAST` can move an existing row's `created_at` EARLIER, only when the same (hash, tenant) registers again; it blanks and drops nothing. The backfill NEVER updates an existing row.

## The backfill is not run by this PR

- It **writes data** when run with `--apply`.
- It was tested **only on a disposable local PostgreSQL 15 cluster** (databases created and dropped by the cells).
- **Running it on kintsugi, demo or any live environment waits for Kam's word.** Demo is frozen (card `secuura-ks1401-058-merge-demo-billing-1104` = a). Nothing in this PR runs it on a deploy: it is a script, not a migration.
- **Before running it, the operator reads** the script's header (what it writes, what it excludes, exit codes) and runs it once WITHOUT `--apply`: the dry run prints, per tenant, the documents read and the rows it would write, then a `KS1991_BACKFILL SUMMARY` line. It needs `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` and `DATABASE_URL`, and `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB=true` where tenants have their own databases.
- Measured on the scratch cluster: a tenant with no `tenant_config` row, on a deployment whose `DATABASE_URL` port is not 5432, is read on port 5432 by `TenantPoolManager` (see Findings); the script reports such a tenant as failed and exits 1, and writes nothing for it.

## Behaviour change

Document creation in a multi-tenant deployment now waits for the cross-tenant registration and logs `KS-1991 REGISTRY_WRITE_FAILED` when it fails, still answering 201. The cross-tenant verify rank uses the document's own creation time for rows written after this change and rows the backfill writes. A new backfill exists and is not run by this PR on any environment.

## Residuals (not changed here)

- Registry rows written late BEFORE this change keep their late `created_at` (the backfill never updates a row). How many exist anywhere is UNMEASURED.
- Whether any live environment holds an unregistered original, a late row or an `sha256:`-prefixed duplicate pair is UNMEASURED.
- The certification path still does not register; after a backfill, a new certification row is unregistered until the next run (a copy that is not in the registry is never presented cross-tenant).

## Test Evidence

**Touched (11 files).** `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts` (registerInPlatformRegistry; a comment in crossTenantLookup), `routes/verificationV2.ts` (a comment in crossTenantRowsByHash), `routes/documents.ts` (the awaited registration, the idempotent re-POST path); new `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/backfill-platform-registry.js`; new tests `src/__tests__/ks1991-the-create-awaits-its-registration.test.ts`, `ks1991-registry-write-rejects-and-carries-the-documents-clock.test.ts`, `ks1991-registry-backfill.integration.test.ts`, `ks1991-registry-original-rank.integration.test.ts`, `helpers/ks1991PgCluster.ts`; one fragment pair `Projects Documents/fragments/{flow,cheat}/KS-1991-registry-awaited-and-backfilled.html`.

**Ran** (Apple Silicon Mac, macOS 27.2, shared with other agent sessions; **Node v26.8.1, not an LTS line**; PostgreSQL 15.19, a disposable cluster on 127.0.0.1 whose databases the cells create and drop):
- Red first, predictions written before each run. Unit, 12 cells: on the unchanged code 9 red on their predicted assertions, 3 pins green; after the change 12 of 12 pass.
- Integration (`npm run test:integration`, `KS1991_PG_ADMIN_URL` set), 33 cells: the rank file (10 cells, the real v1 `/verify`, `verify-file` and v2 routers over HTTP) read 6 red and 4 pins green on the unchanged code; the backfill file (23 cells on BOTH registry declarations) was red only because the script did not exist. After the change 33 of 33 pass. Five harness corrections on the way, each recorded with its cause (a time-zone rendering, `verify-file`'s known `sha256:` form gap made a pin, a type cast, a zero-fraction literal, and a `main()` cell split in two after it exposed the tenant-pool port finding below).
- Mutants, 21 declared before the run (5 on the create route, 1 on the registration function, 8 on the backfill, 4 on the clock and the upsert, 3 that revert one rank site each: `verification.ts` readCrossTenantOriginals, crossTenantLookup, and `verificationV2.ts` crossTenantRowsByHash): every one turned its named cells red. One declaration was too wide: the dry-run mutant only matters when no flag is passed, so it reached the cell that passes none and not the two `main()` cells.
- The whole originate unit suite: 222 suites, 2604 tests, all pass (24 s).
- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` for originate: rc 0. A `tsc` that includes the five new test files: rc 0; its planted type error is caught.
- eslint on the 8 touched originate files: 0 problems; a planted unused variable is reported.
- `node Blockchain/Dev/scripts/docs-fragments.mjs check`: OK. A planted typed section number in the new flow fragment: FAIL, 2 findings. Its two ADVISORY lines are the same with the new fragments removed (they predate this PR).
- The repo's pre-push hook: ran on the real push (1101 s, 2026-11-10 01:05:32Z to 01:23:53Z): "Blockchain/Dev changes detected"; **PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE: 13 of 16 legs ran, legs 3, 4 and 8 SKIPPED (local stack not up). Nothing failed. Not a pass.** Leg 16 (the test-file type-check ratchet) does not cover originate; the tests-included `tsc` above does.

**NOT run.** The four platform suites (Schemathesis, Akto, Playwright, k6) and any live stack: no stack was up in this session. No deployed environment was touched, and the backfill was run on no environment but the disposable cluster.

**Migrations and config.** None. No migration, no schema change, no spec change, no new environment variable for the services. The backfill reads `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_URL` and `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB`, which originate already has.

## Findings for the board (not fixed here)

1. `packages/shared/src/db/tenant-pool-manager.ts` (refreshConfigs, `dbPort: row.db_port || 5432`): with per-tenant databases on, a tenant that has no `tenant_config` row is read on port 5432 even when `DATABASE_URL` names another port, so it is not recognised as the default database and gets a pool on 5432. Measured on the scratch cluster (port 55523): `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432` for the two unconfigured tenants. Deployments on 5432 do not see it. The backfill reports such a tenant as failed and exits 1.
2. The certification path (`routes/certifications.ts`, `repositories/certificationRepo.ts`) still does not register in the platform registry (ruled out of this PR); the backfill repairs its rows once, and a re-run repairs later ones. A follow-up candidate: register on that path too.
3. `verify-file` with no local row hands crossTenantLookup the `sha256:`-prefixed hash, which matches no bare registry row, so it answers not found on both the old and the new code. Already tracked as KS 1590; measured again here and pinned by a cell.

The gateway would store such a key: `express.json` makes `__proto__` an own key, the merge `{ ...defaults, ...existing, ...body }` in `PUT /api/admin/settings` keeps it, the write stores it, and the GET serves it back. Gate 256 measured the page half; no gadget was found and none was looked for. Verified at source by Wednesday's verifier on 2026-11-10; read in code and run on mocks, not on a live box.

- Page module: `flattenSettings` gives no form value for a stored category or field of those names, and `buildSettingsUpdate` puts a form key naming one into `refused`, the module's own pattern for a key the page cannot send.

**A deviation from the confirmed plan, accepted by Wednesday and put here for the gate to read.** The plan named `resolveTenantId(req)` for the non-platform tenant. That helper returns the token's `organizationId`, and an organization id is not a tenant id since migration 017 (organizations carry their own `tenant_id`); the counts filter the tenant column. So the non-platform tenant is `req.user.tenantId`, the claim originate verified itself (`JwtPayload.tenantId`, `middleware/auth.ts`), the same claim `adminConfig.ts` already passes as `callerTenantId` to the key-revoke policy (line 1193 at develop). ## Refs KS-1516: the opentimestamps and blockchain timestamp types report verified false on creation and on verify

**TIER 1 (proposed): an evidentiary path and a LIVE API change.** `services/timestamping/src/index.ts` (+9 -2, four hunks) plus one new test file (+124 -0). The held Spark patch is applied exactly as it came: 10,741 bytes, sha256 `8c3147511b5e1168`, strict apply at this develop, no edit by me. Kam's ruling a on KS-1516 (card `secuura-ks1516-unverified-timestamp-claims-1102`, 2026-11-02): report `verified: false` for both types until a real check exists.

**What changes in LIVE behaviour, stated first:**
- **A stored row whose STORED type is `opentimestamps` or `blockchain`, with `verified = true`, now answers `verified: false` on `/api/timestamps/verify` whatever `timestampType` the caller sends, and no longer returns its `timestamp` and `tsaUrl` fields** (the answer is `{ verified: false, reason }`: returned before any database lookup when the caller sends one of the two types, and right after the lookup when the caller sends `rfc3161` for such a row; the second case is fix round 1 of 2, below).
- **A forged proof with no stored row** (the right hash plus one attestation, or a chain and slot) used to answer `verified: true` and now answers `verified: false`.
- **Creation** of an `opentimestamps` or `blockchain` timestamp answers `verified: false` and INSERTs `verified = false` with no `verified_at`; it answered and stored `true` before.
- **`rfc3161` is unchanged** for creation, for a forged token with no row, and for a stored `rfc3161` row verified under `rfc3161`. **The one mismatched-type case that changed:** a stored `rfc3161` row verified under the type `opentimestamps` or `blockchain` now answers `false` (develop answered `true`); `false` is the safe direction and only a caller who mislabels the type sees it.

Linear: https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1516 (High, Backlog). This PR says Refs: the ticket stays open.

## Summary

- **The four hunks:** one existing comment reworded; `verified = false` after the `opentimestamps` case and after the `blockchain` case in `createTimestamp`; an early return in `verifyTimestamp` for the two types.
- **Tests:** one new file with 10 cells: 6 that fail on develop without the product change (create x2, a forged verify with no stored row x2, a stored `verified` row x2) and 4 controls (rfc3161 creation, a proof with no attestations, an rfc3161 stored row still verifying, an rfc3161 forged token still refused).
- **Carried flags from the held pass, stated as they are:**
  - The old per-type decode switch for these two types in `verifyTimestamp` is now **dead code and was left in**; this PR does not remove it.
  - **Not in this PR (residue):** (a) the rows already stored as `verified = true`: a read-only count per environment first, classified by proof shape, then an approval-class backfill that is Kam's (the ticket says the count SQL went to the deploy seat); (b) the `supportedTypes` and OpenAPI text, which still advertise both types and a boolean `verified`; (c) the sentence in `Blockchain/Dev/CONNECTORS.md` (line 90 at this develop) that names this deviation and now goes stale; (d) the ticket's options b and c.
- **Live clients of `verified` for these two types, searched here (the held pass did not):** read-only `git grep` over the tree at develop `d0b4825cc244` (a planted positive, `supportedTypes`, returned 2 hits; a string that is not there returned 0). No frontend, package, SDK, website, Outlook add-in, mobile, connector or MCP directory names `/api/timestamps`, `/timestamps` or `timestampType` (0 hits in each). The hits outside the service itself are: the gateway proxy and two gateway tests, the OpenAPI spec and docs, `tests/load/k6-load-test.js` (creates one timestamp with no `timestampType` and checks only a 2xx status), `scripts/smoke-test.sh` and `systemTest` (both create `rfc3161` timestamps only; the smoke test's `verified` check at line 249 is the document verify route). So in this repository nothing reads `verified` for these two types. **UNMEASURED:** callers outside this repository (Platform S, customers, any integration), and what any environment's data holds; what would close it is the platform owners' word and a read-only request log per environment.

## Fix round 1 of 2 (gate 298, NO GO on the first head; Wednesday's ruling under Kam's card)

New commit `e3534ff2ad91` on top of the first head `990efc316091` (no rebase, no force), three files, +24 -4. The whole PR is now 3 files: `index.ts` +13 -2, the ks1516 test +140 -0, `ks753-mock-tsa-fallback-is-not-verified.test.ts` +2 -2. What the gate found and what changed:

- **Gate finding 1 (Medium), fixed:** the stored-row path answered `verified: true` for a stored `opentimestamps` or `blockchain` row when the caller sent `timestampType: "rfc3161"`, because the early return keys on the caller's type and the lookup matches on hash and proof only. Develop answered true there too (not a regression), but it made the first head's sentence "a stored row ... reads false for every caller" untrue. After the lookup, a row whose STORED type is one of the two types now answers `{ verified: false, reason }` whatever type was sent. Cells R7 and R8 are red on the first head (with the test edits and not the product edit: 2 of 13 failed) and green now (13 of 13).
- **Gate finding 2 (Low), stated:** exactly which mismatched-type cases answer false: (1) a stored `opentimestamps` or `blockchain` row, whatever type the caller sends; (2) a stored `rfc3161` row verified under the type `opentimestamps` or `blockchain` (the caller's type hits the early return; develop answered true). `false` is the safe direction, and only a caller who mislabels the type sees it. Control C5 pins (2); a stored `rfc3161` row verified under `rfc3161` is unchanged (control C3).
- **Gate finding 3 (Low), fixed:** R1 and R2 pay the cold app import and RSA key generation, so each has an explicit 20,000 ms timeout (the file had no other explicit timeout to match). One run here took 14.7 s for R1 under load.
- **Gate finding 4 (Info), fixed:** the header comment of `ks753-mock-tsa-fallback-is-not-verified.test.ts` (lines 17 and 18) no longer says the two types keep their behaviour. Comment only; no open PR touches that file (census 0).

## Refs KS-716: the secrets.example.yml comment says an absent system_admin block also removes the super-admin endpoints from scan coverage

**TIER 2 (proposed): comment-only, one YAML file.** Seven comment lines change (+6 -1) in `systemTest/akto/config/secrets.example.yml`. No code, no test, nothing under `Blockchain/Dev`.

Linear: https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-716

## Summary

- **What was wrong.** The comment on the optional `system_admin` block said that, when absent, "that one role is skipped (best-effort)". That is true and incomplete. `harTraffic.ts` sets `adminToken` to null unless both `systemAdminEmail` and `systemAdminPassword` are set, and with no admin token the HAR replay has no fallback for an endpoint the issuer token cannot reach.
- **What it says now.** The block is also the HAR replay's admin fallback. Absent, every endpoint the issuer token cannot get a 2xx from keeps no captured sample, stays a spec-imported placeholder that Akto's `api_selection_filters` exclude from the authz templates, and the scan reports green over it. The line below it no longer lists `system_admin` as simply optional: it is optional for the setup seed, not for scan coverage.
- **Scope: item 2 of the ticket only** ("correct the `secrets.example.yml` comment to state the coverage consequence"). Item 1 (a loud warning when `adminToken` is null) and item 3 (assert the relative-versus-absolute URL split) are NOT done. The ticket (Todo, High) stays open.
- **Held patch** (a Spark pass, 1,451 B, sha256 prefix `d625095d8f53`): applied strictly at develop `d0b4825cc244`, and the applied hunks are byte-identical to it (`cmp` rc 0). Nothing was changed by this seat.

## Test plan / Test Evidence

**Touched:** one file, `systemTest/akto/config/secrets.example.yml` (+6 -1; the repo-root `systemTest/` folder, not `Blockchain/Dev`). Base is develop `d0b4825cc244`. **Ran** (Seat R 93rd, 2026-11-10, Apple Silicon Mac, macOS 27.2):
- **Comment-only proof,** by my own tool: every line whose first non-blank character is `#` is dropped from the file before and after; the remaining text is identical (sha256 prefix `c94297c0ba45f391` on both, 41 lines each). Controls beside it: the same text plus one code line differs; plus one comment line it stays identical. All 7 changed lines start with `#` after the diff marker.
- **Non-ASCII:** the added lines carry 2 non-ASCII characters (an arrow `⇒` and an em dash), as the held patch does.
- **The claim about `harTraffic.ts`, quoted from the file at develop `d0b4825cc244`:** lines 130 to 138 read `const adminToken = config.systemAdminEmail && config.systemAdminPassword ? await getSecuuraToken(config, config.systemAdminEmail, config.systemAdminPassword, 'system admin (HAR replay)') : null;` (the condition is on line 131, the `null` on line 138; the function returns it on line 139).
- **Two more claims in the new comment, read against the code (read, not run):** (1) the placeholder mechanism (`responseCode: -1` and `api_selection_filters`) is described the same way in the headers of `harTraffic.ts` (lines 5 and 6) and `aktoTraffic.ts` (line 20). (2) "the scan reports green over it": `adminToken` is read in only one place outside the tests, `harReplay.ts` line 339; `harReplaySurface.ts` prints its COVERAGE DEGRADED line only for a skipped replay (no issuer session), so a missing admin token with a live issuer prints nothing. `harReplay.ts` lines 324 to 338 already say the same in a comment ("SILENTLY").
- **Where the figure "0 of 16" lives.** The new comment says "KS-716 measured 0 of 16 super-admin-only endpoints scanned without this block", as the held patch has it. That figure is in the ticket's DESCRIPTION, section "Measured - 2026-08-29, local slot-1 stack, Akto 2.22.2" (written by the ticket's creator: "relative: 0 / 16, absolute: 46 / 80 sampled"). It is NOT in a ticket comment. The ticket's one comment (2026-09-30) is a different observation: with a deliberately invalid issuer token the system-admin fallback fed 76 samples, the same as a normal run. The run behind the figure is 10 weeks old and was not re-run by anyone this session: UNMEASURED today. `harReplay.ts` lines 324 to 338 already quote the same figure and attribute it to the ticket's author, so the held comment duplicates that block and does not contradict it.
- **A wording point for the gate.** The ticket's description splits the 16 into 7 analytics paths that are excluded on purpose (`VOLATILE_PATH_RE`, KS 357) and 9 that nothing excludes and the replay persona cannot reach. "0 of 16 super-admin-only endpoints" is the ticket's own headline, not that split. Raised as held, not edited.

- Any Akto run, so the 0 of 16 is not re-measured and no run shows the new comment's claims on a live scan.

- An anonymous verify, and a verify from another tenant, no longer reveal another customer's details: the title, the issuer, `certification.certifiedBy`, the certifier's organisation id (`certification.certifierOrganizationId`) and, on chain-first answers, `onChainMetadata`.

- `verified`, the checks, integrity, the anchor facts and the certification's id, type and time do not change.
- A caller still sees its own tenant's rows named. In production an anonymous caller IS the default tenant (`index.ts:264-266`, `utils/requestTenant.ts:45-52`), so on a single-tenant deployment (demo, local) a row of the default tenant still names itself to it.
- The change a demo user can see: a hash known ONLY to the chain (another environment's document) still verifies, but no longer names its issuer, its organisation id or its on-chain metadata.
- In multi-tenant mode, cross-tenant answers also lose the organisation id.
- The anchored transaction's own metadata stays public on Cardano at the `txHash` the answer still returns. This PR does not and cannot change that.

- card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` = a (2026-11-09 13:44:07), pack row 16, option 1, "withhold all four";

- **Gap 1, the organisation id.**
  - Before: `scopeTenantFields` (:463) nulled title, issuer and `certifiedBy`, never `certifierOrganizationId`.

In production this fires only on reads that omit the column, and every verify read that feeds the check now selects it. ## Refs KS-784: the Teams webhook address is checked before the Microsoft 365 configuration

**TIER 1: an outbound-request guard (as ruled).** One route in `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts` changes the order of its checks; one comment in the same file is corrected; eight new cells; two docs fragments.

Linear: https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-784

## Summary

- **The defect.** `POST /api/teams/webhook-config` ran `requireM365` first, as route middleware (index.ts line 1276 at develop `204e62acdc35`). It answers 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` whenever `ENTRA_CLIENT_ID`, `ENTRA_CLIENT_SECRET` or `ENTRA_TENANT_ID` is unset, which is every developer stack and slot. So the outbound-address guard inside the handler (`assertSafeOutboundUrl`: https only; no loopback, private, link-local or internal host, nor anything resolving to one) could not be reached there, the Schemathesis `pr` sweep saw a permanent 503 for this operation, and the systemTest regression for the guard (KS 502 section 3b, `tests/test_webhook_ssrf.py`) has been a skip. The ticket calls the guard `validateWebhookUrl`; at develop it is `assertSafeOutboundUrl` from `@secuura/shared`.
- **The ruling.** Kam's card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` = a (2026-11-09 13:44:07), pack row A2, option 1: validate the address before the configuration check.
- **The order now**, accepted by the coordinator: the caller's organisation (`requireCallerOrg`, 403), then the body schema (400 "Validation failed") and `assertSafeOutboundUrl` (400 "webhookUrl rejected: ..."), both unchanged, then `requireM365` itself, called inside the handler so the 503 body is the same, then the insert. The caller's organisation stays first, as KS 1673 put it ("authority first, before the body is even parsed").
- **Two consequences, ruled and stated:** a token with no organisation on an unconfigured stack now gets 403 instead of 503 (pinned by cell R5); and on an unconfigured stack a hostname `webhookUrl` is now resolved (DNS) before the 503. A valid address on an unconfigured stack still gets the 503 and stores nothing (cell C1). No other route changes: `requireM365` stays the middleware of every other route that had it.
- **A comment corrected in the same file.** `POST /api/teams/notify`'s KS 487 note said registration "is gated behind requireM365 (so it is unreachable wherever Entra is unconfigured)". After this change the registration's address check runs, but the insert is still stopped, so it now says registration "stores nothing wherever Entra is unconfigured".
- The cheat and flow fragments for this change are included.

## Test plan / Test Evidence

**Touched:** 4 files. `Blockchain/Dev/services/m365-integration/src/index.ts` (+15 -3: the route line, the in-handler check with its comment, the notify comment), the new suite `src/__tests__/ks784-teams-webhook-address-checked-before-m365-config.test.ts` (+157), and two fragments `Projects Documents/fragments/{cheat,flow}/KS-784-teams-webhook-address-checked-before-m365-config.html`. One commit on develop `204e62acdc35`.

**Ran** (Seat R 91st, 2026-11-09, Apple Silicon Mac, macOS 27.2, Node v26.8.1, which is NOT an LTS line; `packages/shared` rebuilt first):
- **Eight cells, prediction written before any run.** They use the REAL `assertSafeOutboundUrl` (not mocked): every address is an IP literal, for which the guard's resolver returns without a DNS lookup. `../db` is mocked to count INSERTs, `authenticate` sets the caller, and `ENTRA_*` is set per request only in the configured cells (`isConfigured()` reads it on every call).
  - On develop, exactly the five predicted cells were red, each answering `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`: R1 link-local `https://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/`, R2 loopback `https://127.0.0.1/hook`, R3 `http://` to a public address, R4 a malformed address, R5 a token with no organisation. Fixed: 400 `webhookUrl rejected` (R1-R3), 400 `Validation failed` (R4), 403 `Token carries no organisation` (R5), nothing stored.
  - Three controls green on both trees: C1 a valid public https address on an unconfigured stack gets requireM365's exact 503 body and stores nothing; C2 on a configured stack the same address is stored for the caller's organisation (201); C3 on a configured stack a link-local address is refused 400.
- **Mutants, declared before running, file restored and hash-checked after each:** putting `requireM365` back on the route (and removing the in-handler call) turns exactly R1-R5 red; removing the configuration check altogether turns exactly C1 red.
- **m365-integration suite** (vitest): 303 of 303, 76 files; the 295 cells on develop are all present with the same result.
- **Type checks:** `tsc --noEmit` over the service: 0 errors. The test-file ratchet (`scripts/typecheck-tests/check.cjs services/m365-integration`, hook leg 16): 32 test files examined, 0 errors, 0 new.
- **Spec:** `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` already declares 400, 403 and 503 for this operation; no spec change.
- **Docs fragments.** `docs-fragments.mjs check` ends in `OK`.

**NOT run:**
- Any request to a running stack (no stack up); the four platform suites; Schemathesis.
- The systemTest side named below.
- Node 24.

**Migrations + config:** none.

**Pre-push hook:** (quoted from the push of this head by Seat R 91st)
```
PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.
  legs 3 4 8 — local stack not up; you can clear this by starting it.
  This is NOT a pass. Do not quote it as one — say which legs ran.
```
- Leg 14, verbatim: `shell suites: 123 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (of 123)`

## Before this deploys

- m365-integration changes behaviour on stacks without Microsoft 365 configured: an invalid or unsafe address now gets 400, and a token with no organisation 403, where both got 503. Configured stacks are unchanged. Demo is frozen; nothing deploys from this PR.

## Notes for the gate

- **Callers, before and after.** The api-gateway proxies `/api/teams` to m365-integration unchanged. The admin portal's `M365SetupWizard.tsx` posts here; on a configured stack it sees what it saw before. The existing ks1673 and ks1364 suites (configured, guard mocked; and the spec) pass unchanged. systemTest: `schemathesis.toml` names this operation, and `config/check_predicates.py` treats a declared 503 from unconfigured integrations as expected; in positive mode Schemathesis will now see the declared 400 for most generated addresses. `tests/test_webhook_ssrf.py`'s KS 502 section 3b skip says the route "stays 503-gated by requireM365"; after this merges that reason is false and the skip can become the plain red-to-green test the ticket describes. Those systemTest files are the follow-up, not this PR. The USER_TESTING harness scripts and `systemTest/inline-runner/runner.js` also name the path; not read further.
- **Open pull requests on these files:** PR 2080 (KS 1670, head `83ee8509c985`) also edits `index.ts` (hunks at lines 555, 685, 865 and 1170; this PR's start at develop lines 1276, 1294 and 1489). Editing the file while 2080 is open was granted by the coordinator for this push: the census at 04:53:12Z found no other open PR on these four paths, and a predicted merge of this head with 2080's head is clean, all 19 of 2080's added lines next to these. **BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, FIRST:** the 401 applies on OPTIONAL mounts too. A request on a public route that presents such a token now gets 401 instead of being served as anonymous; a request with no token is unchanged. Cell C9 pins the first half (no `userId` on the optional mount: 401, 0 upstream hits), cell C16 the second (no token on the same mount: 200, served). Wednesday's ruling 2026-11-09 04:09:18Z, on the KS 1198 reasoning: a pass-through on an optional mount would forward the verified Bearer upstream.

**What round 2 changed: the tenant refusal is OUT of this PR.** Round 1 also carried the tenant ticket (KS 619): a token with no tenant was refused unless its role was SUPER_ADMIN or SYSTEM_ADMIN. The tier-1 gate (285, finding G285-1) found that the platform-admin login mints whatever role the `platform_admins` row stores (`platform_admin`, `platform_viewer`, or `admin` from the Azure migrate default) with no tenant, and that the token carries no claim, issuer, audience or key id that marks it as that login's. So round 1 locked those logins out of every gateway route, public ones included. Kam ruled the split (card `secuura-ks619-platform-admin-login-no-marker-1109` = a): this PR keeps only the user-id and role guard, and the tenant ticket becomes its own change, in which the platform-admin login stamps one claim and the gateway excepts it. Cells T1 to T3 pin that a platform-admin-login token with no tenant is served (red against round 1's code, green now); a tenantless token is served in the default tenant exactly as on develop.

Kam's card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` = a, row A3 (KS-1208):

That also closes the ticket's N-1 comment (a present claim holding U+0142 or CR-LF also answered 500). Falsy optional claims keep today's drop.

## Refs KS-785: start-environment.sh lets compose read the checked passwords from .env, so the credential check and compose agree

**TIER 1: the credential start path (Urgent). ROUND 2 of 2**, after gate 283's NO GO. `start-environment.sh` gains one guarded loop that unsets two shell exports before `docker compose up`; `check-slot-credentials.sh` changes comments only; new cells; two docs fragments.

Linear: https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-785

## Summary

- **The defect.** `check-slot-credentials.sh` reports the `.env` value of `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `REDIS_PASSWORD` (it sources the file in a subshell). `docker compose` takes a value exported in the shell over the project `.env`. `start-local.sh` sources `.env` before compose; `start-environment.sh` did nothing. So in a shell that still exported the old shared passwords, the checker printed per-clone for a rotated `.env` and exited 0 while compose got the shared passwords.
- **What changed from round 1, and why.** Round 1 made `start-environment.sh` source `.env` before compose. Gate 283 refused it: on a fresh clone the start died at the shipped `env.example` line 236 (`ISSUER_NAME=Secuura Platform`, bash runs `Platform`, rc 127, compose never reached: **G283-1**); a malformed `.env` line printed secret text and stopped the start (**G283-2**); `bash -x` traced every value (G283-3); and every other export (slot, ports, `NODE_ENV`) changed for compose and the services (G283-4).
- **The ruled shape (the coordinator's, inside Kam's KS-785 ruling).** `start-environment.sh` never executes `.env`: no `source`, no `.`, no `set -a`. For exactly the keys the checker reads (`POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `REDIS_PASSWORD`, its lines 171-172, the only two) and only where `.env` assigns the key, it `unset`s the shell export before `docker compose up`, so compose falls through to its own `.env` read and gets the value the checker reported. The match is a line match, `^(export[[:space:]]+)?KEY=`; the value is never read. The `export` form is a declared widening of the ruling's `^KEY=`: the checker accepts `export KEY=` lines, and real Compose reads them from its env file (measured below). Keys `.env` does not assign keep the shell's value, as on develop.
- **What an operator sees.** On the next start, a stale shell export of either password no longer reaches compose when `.env` sets that password; compose uses the `.env` value the checker reported. Nothing else changes: every other export reaches compose and the `npm run dev` services exactly as on develop (G283-4 is answered by construction), a malformed or unreadable `.env` no longer stops this script (the checker still warns, non-blocking), and nothing from `.env` is printed or traced.
- **The checker: comment only** (its 154 non-comment lines are identical to develop's, with a planted code line that differs and a planted comment that does not). One hunk, develop lines 109-112, inside the ruled 102-125 window: the KS-785 paragraph now says what the start paths guarantee (G283-6). Round 1's other comment change is gone, because it is false again under this shape.
- The cheat and flow fragments are rewritten to this shape.

## Test plan / Test Evidence

**Touched:** (round 2, against develop `4d6b7bb17fd3`) `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/start-environment.sh` (+19: the loop and its comment), `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-slot-credentials.sh` (+11 -4, comment only), `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/check_slot_credentials.test.sh` (+191: 14 cells, their fixture and stub), and the two fragments. Two commits on the branch: round 1 `190ffa868d7d` and round 2 `7dc6ff72cf61`, which replaces round 1's `source` (no force, no rebase).

**Ran** (Seat R 91st, 2026-11-09, Apple Silicon Mac, macOS 27.2, /bin/bash 3.2.57, Docker Compose v5.5.0, Node v26.8.1, which is NOT an LTS line):
- **Real Compose, render-only** (`config`, a scratch fixture via `--env-file`, no containers, no real `.env`): a sentinel export beats the fixture; no export, the fixture wins; an exported but empty variable also beats the fixture; an unexported shell variable is invisible to compose; an `export POSTGRES_PASSWORD=...` line in the env file is read.
- **Fourteen KS-785 cells** run the REAL `start-environment.sh` and the REAL checker in a fixture tree; every other command is a stub on PATH, and the `docker` stub reads values the way Compose was measured to, recording what it got at `compose up` (rc 97). Predictions were written before each run (round 2's file records two post-run deltas, both in my predictions, not in the code).
  - At round 1's head, exactly these were red: **G283-1** (a `.env` made from the shipped template with both passwords filled: rc 127, compose not reached), **G283-2** (`REDIS_PASSWORD=FXSECRETfirst FXSECRETtail`: rc 127 and the secret's tail printed), **G283-3** (under `bash -x`, 2 traced value lines), **G283-4** (exported slot, ports and `NODE_ENV` replaced by `.env`'s), and **KEYS** (the script's key list must equal the checker's). Now: G283-1 `CLEAN|rotated_fx_pg_A1|rotated_fx_redis_A1|rc97`; G283-2 `rc97`, 0 secret text in the output; G283-3 0 traced values; G283-4 the shell's values reach compose unchanged (the slot-2 ports computed from the slot-1 bases); KEYS equal.
  - **G283-K** (`.env` assigns no `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`: the shell's export reaches compose, as the checker also reads it) is green at both heads; only the unconditional-unset mutant reddens it.
  - The three original KS-785 cells and four controls: red on develop exactly as in round 1 (develop's script also reddens G283-1 and G283-K, because both export values the develop script never unsets), green now.
  - Suite: **46 of 46**; the 32 develop cells keep their labels and results. `ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh` 78 of 78. `check-stack-safety.sh`: 110 invariants hold.
- **Mutants**, each applied in place, the suite run, the file restored and hash-checked: develop's script reddens the 3 KS-785 cells plus G283-1, G283-K and KEYS; round 1's `source` block reddens G283-1, -2, -3, -4 and KEYS; widening the list to every key `.env` assigns reddens G283-4 and KEYS; dropping the line match (unset unconditionally) reddens G283-K.
- **`docs-fragments.mjs check`:** `OK`.

**NOT run:**
- The start path against any real stack, container or real `.env` (fixtures only, by rule); shellcheck (not installed); the four platform suites; leg 14 locally for round 2 (the hook runs it).

  legs 3 4 8 — local stack not up; you can clear this by starting it.

## Before this deploys

- Nothing deploys: a developer start script, a checker comment, a suite and docs. Team members who run `start-environment.sh` get the new behaviour on their next pull.

The census before the push and the merge tree with PR 2052's head are in the READY.

## Refs KS-2109: the gateway's index.ts names the real tenant-override check

**TIER 1: a comment in the gateway's auth path (as ruled).** Comment only: one comment in `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` and two docs fragments. Not one code byte moves.

Linear: https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-2109

## Summary

- **What was stale.** The EXCEPTION paragraph above the middleware that strips trust headers at the edge explains why `x-tenant-override` is let through: the auth middleware decides whether to honour it. It said the middleware "enforces SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES gating" and cited `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:380-382`, "the `SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES.includes(decoded.role)` check inside the post-jwt.verify block". At develop `4d6b7bb17fd3`, `SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES` has 0 matches in `auth.ts` (control: `isPlatformRole` has 2), and `jwt.verify` has 0 matches too (control: `verifyRs256` has 4). KS 1536 replaced the list; the token is now verified by `verifyRs256(token)` (line 651, under `// Verify JWT`).
- **What it says now**, written from the code at that develop: the middleware honours the header only when `tenantOverride && isPlatformRole(decoded.role)` (line 697), the check that follows `verifyRs256(token)`, and `isPlatformRole` comes from `@secuura/shared` (`PLATFORM_ROLES` = SYSTEM_ADMIN and SUPER_ADMIN, `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts` lines 60 and 140). The comment names the expression, keeps the old advice to grep it if the line moves, and one closing sentence records what it used to cite and why it changed.
- **The lines, exactly.** Before (index.ts 326-331 at develop):

  ```
  // through 2026-05-09) and made KS-4 (BUG-ISOLATION-001) untestable. Auth
  // middleware enforces SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES gating before honouring the value

  // `SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES.includes(decoded.role)` check inside the post-jwt.verify
  // block — grep that expression if the line moves), so letting it pass through
  // the edge strip is safe.
  ```

  After (326-333):

  ```
  // through 2026-05-09) and made KS-4 (BUG-ISOLATION-001) untestable. Auth
  // middleware honours the value only for a platform role: the
  // `tenantOverride && isPlatformRole(decoded.role)` check that follows
  // `verifyRs256(token)` in services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts
  // (isPlatformRole is from @secuura/shared: SYSTEM_ADMIN and SUPER_ADMIN; grep
  // that expression if the line moves), so letting it pass through the edge
  // strip is safe. (KS-2109: this comment used to cite SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES at
  // auth.ts:380-382; KS-1536 replaced that list with isPlatformRole.)
  ```

  The diff is 5 lines out and 7 in (the stat's 12); the rewritten sentence is 8 lines counted from the unchanged one that starts it.
- **Scope.** This is the first bullet of KS-2109's item 3 (index.ts lines 327 to 329; line 328 was stale too and is covered). The other two pointers are PR 2111 (`utils/trustHeaders.ts` and the agent document-operation rules), which does not touch this file; no wait on it, as ruled.

The callers do not treat `false` alike: `adminConfig.ts` line 1650 (`POST /api/admin/rights-holders/:id/invite`) reads the answer and reports `emailSent`; line 1516 drops it (fire-and-forget); and the notification client's SMTP fallback (`notificationClient.ts` lines 79 to 123) awaits the send, does not read the answer, and logs `Notification sent via SMTP fallback`. Each catch now reads the message inside a `try` and logs the text, or the constant `unreadable thrown value`. A hostile value takes the path an ordinary Error already takes: `getAcsClient` returns `null`, the two send catches return `false`, `sendEmail` resolves `false`. The log text for an ordinary Error is unchanged, and a missing message on an Error-like value (`undefined` or `null`) is logged as before. A thrown `null` or `undefined` itself differs by catch (measured in round 1, base `c0e6e744b7b2` against this branch, 18 cells): the two ACS catches resolve `false` and log `undefined` on both trees; the SMTP catch rejected on base (a `TypeError` from `error.message`) and now resolves `false` and logs `unreadable thrown value`.
