Refs KS-2060

**BLUF.** After an erasure, the user's wallet is gone from the users row, and from governance unless a legacy participant row (one whose id is not the user's id) holds it or a stale write puts it back (see Stated limits). The erasure clears the user's own participant row (the one whose id is the user's id): its wallet, stake, power, flags and did. Delegations to and from it are revoked, and refused from then on. The user's address is blanked from proposals, votes and delegations, while tallies, ids and stored power are kept. Migration 059 lets the three address columns hold NULL. **TIER 1** (a data-destroying path: migration 059 and the erasure cascade's governance writes), its own gate.

**Rulings this implements.** Kam's card on the ticket (2026-11-06): keep the row for audit, clear its wallet and vote power, and clear the wallet on the users row. Kam's two cards of 2026-11-08, option a both:
- `secuura-ks2060-clear-wallet-null-migration-1106`: "[a] NULL, with migration 059 (recommended)".
- `secuura-ks2060-address-in-history-dpia-1106`: "[a] Remove it from governance history (recommended)", detail "Votes, proposer and delegation addresses blanked on erasure; tallies kept".

The coordinator's rulings: D-3 (revoke both ways), D-4 (by id only), D-6 (consumer group created at `$`), D-7 (did goes too), D-9 (b) (where the users-row clear runs), and the delegation columns in the same 059.

**Four commits.**
1. Seat U 17th. Originate clears `users.wallet_address` after the fan-out's read. Auth's handler clears it as a backstop, and the wallet link route refuses a deactivated caller. Governance subscribes to the erasure event for the first time.
2. Seat U 18th. Migration 059, the row's wallet, history blanking, the delegation refusal, the nullable spec fields, the DPIA tables, and the real-PostgreSQL suite.
3. Seat U 18th. PR 2076 (the KS 2058 follow-up) merged words saying an erased user's row keeps its wallet and vote power and still takes an admin's stake "(KS-2060)", and that erasure leaves the wallet on the users row. Those words now apply only to a user erased before this ships, until the backfill. Comments and fragments only; the S7 cell is unchanged and still passes. This commit also brings the two KS-2060 fragments' figures to this base. The KS 1951 fragments were read and say nothing this change makes false.
4. Seat U 19th. Words only, on our QA gate 266's notes (tier 1, GO WITH NOTES at `0d747d09ab23`): the DPIA and four fragments now name the legacy participant row, the stale-write limit as the gate measured it, and that an event dead-lettered before 059 is lost. Nothing under `services/` changes.

**Base.** Built on develop `c0e6e744b7b2` (PR 2076's squash). The branch was rebased before its first push, and the rebased tree equals merge-tree's prediction. At push time develop was `5302a8025729`. That move changed one file, with no overlap with this branch; the driver's develop gate checked it, and its planted control fired. Commit 4 was pushed with develop at `6220c168cc92`: the move from `c0e6e744b7b2` changed 8 files, none of them on this branch's paths, by the same gate with its planted control.

**Migration 059 is wider than the first card's "one statement".** It holds three `DROP NOT NULL` statements in one file: the participant wallet and both delegation addresses. A marker value instead of NULL was ruled out, because it would read as an address. `UNIQUE(wallet_address)` stays; it admits many NULLs. 059 applies on boot (api-gateway) or through `scripts/run-migrations.sh` once merged. This PR's author has applied it nowhere except scratch databases. 059 has no down migration, and once one erasure has written a NULL, `SET NOT NULL` cannot be restored (our QA gate 266 measured it).

**Two parts go wider than Kam's cards, both on the coordinator's rulings and disclosed here:** 059's three statements (above), and the wallet link refusal, which also stops an admin-disabled user who was never erased (status `inactive` or `deactivated`) from linking until reinstated.

**The generated yaml.** `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` is also changed by PR 2073, a granted overlap. Its head and this one merge clean in either order, to one tree (merge-tree). Whichever of PR 2073 and this PR merges second recomputes the yaml (`npm run generate-openapi`) and runs `npm run check:openapi` on the union before its READY. This PR's yaml change is three nullable fields in the governance schemas.

## Before this deploys
- **059 must reach a box before or with the governance image.** A database without it refuses the new handler's first statement with 23502. The erasure event then fails its three attempts and is dead-lettered (cell E0). This was measured on the compiled services too: a run on a database built before 059 cleared nothing. An event dead-lettered that way is lost, not delayed: nothing replays a dead letter into this handler, so that subject stays uncleared until the backfill.
- Migrations are baked into the `migrations` image (originate's Dockerfile), so that image is rebuilt with the services. Check that the runner prints `Applying 059_ks2060_erased_wallet_and_delegation_addresses_nullable.sql`; a summary line alone does not show it ran.
- The governance image installs `ioredis` from its own manifest (commit 1), so it is rebuilt from this tree.

The same shape loses one of two concurrent votes' tallies, independently of this PR (read in the code, not measured). Reported, not changed here.
- **The quorum denominator** on a proposal open during the erasure stays high by the cleared power until the proposal ends.
- **A failed publish** costs the whole cascade and is not reported (originate's `events.ts`). The users-row wallet still clears. Filed separately.

- **The spec is not the Akto collection.** The three nullable fields are declared, not scanned.

## Refs KS-1209: the audit gates print a malformed baseline expires as malformed, not as missing, and a wrong-type or padded expires is malformed in both validators

**Tier 2, tooling only.** Two audit validators, their two test files, the case-count file and two docs fragments. No service, image, frontend or deploy is touched, and no baseline row, expiry, lock or manifest changes.

Linear: https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1209

## Summary

- **Why this PR exists.** The first KS-1209 PR (merged to develop as a6cd828e820d) made `validateOutOfScope` in `lock-discovery.mjs` report a PRESENT but malformed `expires` as malformed instead of `missing`. This is its follow-up, with the sibling it declared and two more points from the gate on that PR (gate 230). The ticket's own title is about preflight's closing verdict; the malformed-`expires` item is carried in its description ("carried here, not a separate ticket"), and the first PR is attached to it.
- **The printer (the declared sibling).** `printBaselineProblems` in `baseline-contract.mjs` wrote the word "missing" before the whole list, so `audit:gate` and `audit:locks` both told a reader `missing expires (not an ISO YYYY-MM-DD date: "soon")` about a baseline row that visibly has an `expires`. It now prints a missing field on its own line and a malformed expiry on its own line, with the value quoted back. The problems data shape `{ id, missing[] }` and the pinned text "not an ISO YYYY-MM-DD date" are unchanged.
- **Gate 230 F1, wrong-type `expires`.** An `expires` that is present but not a string (a number, a boolean, an array, an object, a Date) took the "absent" branch in BOTH validators and printed `missing expires`, byte-identical to a really absent one, because `nonEmpty` is false for it. Both now report it as malformed, quoting the value; a BigInt, function or symbol, which `JSON.stringify` cannot print, is quoted by its type (`<bigint>`) instead of crashing the gate. `undefined`, `null`, an empty string and a blank string still print `missing`. Ticket: https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1600/ks-1594-follow-up-pull-request-1547-round-2-gate-the-non-string-and

**Proposed tier: 1.** A behaviour change on an authentication-adjacent admin route: originate's `POST /api/admin/api-keys` now refuses a malformed `permissions` value with 400. One source file (+10), one new test file, a docs fragment pair. No migration, no config.

> **Before merging:** the pre-merge suites were **not run** on this PR (Test Evidence, "NOT run"). The boxes below stay unticked; they are not a pass.

### Pre-merge acknowledgment (author)

- [ ] <!--ack:schemathesis--> **Schemathesis** pre-merge sweep run and **passing** (`python3 scripts/run.py pre-merge`): **NOT RUN**
- [ ] <!--ack:akto--> **Akto** pre-merge scan run and **passing** (`npm run test:pre-merge`): **NOT RUN**

### PII review (KS 256 R15/R16)

Not applicable. This PR changes no published spec, example value, fixture, seed data or log line, and it adds no email-shaped string. The one error message it adds, `permissions must be an array of strings`, names a field and contains no caller data.

## What this does

Kam ruled option a on card `secuura-ks1600-originate-malformed-permissions-1106` (2026-11-06 14:58 AEDT): refuse with 400, matching the security service. Item 3 of KS-1600 was the open difference. `POST /api/admin/api-keys` read `permissions` as the array when it was a non-empty array and as `['read']` otherwise, so a bare string or an object fell back to `['read']` and a nested array or an array holding `null` was stored as given. The security service's own door parses `scopes: z.array(z.string())` and answers 400 for the same shapes.

Now a **present** `permissions` that is not an array of strings answers 400 `BAD_REQUEST` ("permissions must be an array of strings") before any INSERT and before the 403 decisions, as the security route also validates before it authorises.

**Unchanged on purpose** (Wednesday's answer to the plan, 2026-11-07): an absent, `null` or empty `permissions` still becomes `['read']`. They are not among the four shapes the ticket names. The security service stores `[]` and refuses `null`, so **two small differences remain**; widening is a separate decision. **The two doors also name the field differently: originate reads `permissions`, the security service reads `scopes`.** "Matching" here means the same validity rule, not the same field, and a body that carries only `scopes` at originate is still ignored and becomes `['read']`. Whether the gateway renames the field is not measured.

## Callers, measured first (the card's condition)

Instrument: `git grep -I` over develop `b27f5fb30f4a`, two passes (the literal `admin/api-keys`: 63 lines in 29 files; `api-keys` in non-test, non-doc source: 32 lines in 13 files, which found two admin pages the first pass missed). Predicate: a request to originate's `POST /api/admin/api-keys` that carries a `permissions` field. **Result: production callers 0** (the admin UI creates keys through `/api/security/keys` with `scopes`); **test and tooling callers 5 files, all sending a string array**; originate's own tests: **23 of 23** payload lines carrying `permissions:` are string arrays. **In-repo senders of a malformed value: 0.** Controls: a nonsense token reads 0 on the same pathspec, the mint route's own file is found by the wide pattern, and a first grep for two constants that read 0 was an instrument failure (git grep takes no `\s`), caught by its positive control.
**Not measured:** callers outside this repository (Platform S, connectors, customer scripts) and live traffic on Kintsugi or demo. A read-only census of `svc_api_keys` rows whose `scopes` are not an array of strings, run by a deploy seat on Kintsugi, would show a past malformed mint (stored inertly); this seat touched no box.

## Overlap with PR 2060

PR 2060 (KS-1536 PR 3a) also changes `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`: two hunks at lines 57 to 80 (`SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES` becomes `isPlatformRole` in `resolveTenantId`). This PR's single block is at line 990, in `POST /api-keys`. A trial merge of this head with PR 2060's head (`796ea55fb8eb`) is **clean** (`git merge-tree --write-tree`, tree `eecb2bad1aba`). **Whichever merges second merges develop in.** The push ran under Wednesday's exact-name overlap grant for that branch at that head.

## Test Evidence

**Touched:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts` (+10); one new test file `services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1600-malformed-permissions-refused-at-the-admin-mint.test.ts` (+147, 17 cells); the KS-1600 item 3 fragment pair. No manifest line (the file sets no anchoring flag).

**Ran** (Seat V 26th, the author). Host: Apple Silicon Mac shared with other seats, Node v26.8.1 (**not an LTS measurement**; no other Node is installed on this host), jest as installed for originate, base develop `b27f5fb30f4a`, 2026-11-07.
- **Test first.** On the unchanged source, **11 of 11 RED cells fail by assertion** (10 received `201` with one INSERT, one received `403` where `400` is wanted; 0 harness errors) and the **6 controls pass** (`evidence/item2_stageA_red_on_develop_01.out`). With the change, **17 of 17 pass**.
- **Mutants: 9 of 9 matched**, the red set declared in the runner before any run: delete the check (11 red); `Array.isArray` only (6); test element 0 only (2); refuse `[]` too (1); refuse `null` too (1); status 422 (11); code `VALIDATION` (11); message changed (10); the check moved after the 403 decisions (1). Each plant restored with sha256 equal and `git status` unchanged (`mutants_ks1600_v26.tsv`).
- Whole originate suite (jest): **219 files / 2596 tests, all pass** (develop plus this PR's 1 file and 17 cells). One run.

## Summary

**Behaviour change, named first. Tier 1, security service.** Nothing is deployed and no box was touched. This is the write side of the boot race, found by QA gate 225 on PR 2046.

A boot race is the state where `DATABASE_URL` is set and the first database probe has not succeeded (`db.ts` retries in the background). With a URL set that is the only way the availability flag is down in production: `closeDb` has no production caller, and no probe runs once the flag is up. A database lost later leaves the flag up. A revoke of a cached key then reaches the 503 through a failing save, but an uncached revoke answers 404 `API key not found`, and by read develop answers the same; this PR does not change that (gate 248, G2).

| In a boot race | develop | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Revoke a key in memory | 200 `API key revoked`, 0 writes; valid again after recovery | **503**, 0 writes; the in-memory revoke is kept |
| Mint | 201 with a key, 0 writes; the key is gone after recovery | **503**, no key material, nothing left in memory |
| Rotate | 201, `priorKeysRevoked: 1`, 0 writes. After recovery the OLD key validates and the NEW key is gone | **503**, no key, no count, nothing changed in memory |
| Revoke a key not in memory | 404 `API key not found` | **503** `The API key could not be read, so it was not revoked` |

Memory-only (`DATABASE_URL` unset or empty) and flag-up answer exactly as before. Validation and the role check still answer first: 400, then the role-level 403, then 503. A foreign admin revoking a key not in memory gets 503, not 403, because the key's tenant cannot be judged yet; develop answered 404 there (gate 248, G4).

**Also here, from the same gate:**
- **N5, both arms.** A validate holding its stored read open overwrote a revoke that landed meanwhile, and the key answered `valid:true`. Both arms now read the current map entry after the await. The miss arm was the gate's open question; red-first shows it has the same overwrite.

## Linear

https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1171

**Deploy owed: anchoring on both boxes; it does NOT go out without Kam's word (the card's option text); demo frozen; nothing done.**

## BLUF for Kam

- **What you ruled:** card `secuura-ks-1171-8k-unconfigured-chain-counts-as-answered-1106` = b, 2026-11-06T14:58:53: "Narrow fix: only the re-poll treats 'no connection' as unknown, never as an answer". Detail: "Consistent with your 09-25 ruling; touches the re-poll only; tier 1 gate; no deploy without your word."
- **Built:** a re-poll with no Blockfrost client now reads as unknown and the row rests. It no longer reads as absent, so no retry and no second fee-paying transaction follow from it.
- **A plain note on scope:** the card says "touches the re-poll only". This touches two more files, the provider and the poller, and changes the behaviour of the re-poll only, with the other callers' readings pinned. The provider is where the two cases have to be told apart; the poller has to carry that to the rule. `index.ts` is untouched.
- **Measured for you, and gone to you through Wednesday:** the fee-paying harm has no route today, by read plus a probe. See "How far the harm reaches". That was the unmeasured premise of option c. Your ruling b stands unless you change it.

## How far the harm reaches

Read at develop plus a probe with the client class and `fetch` both set to throw if touched. Not a proof about future paths.

- Real mode: `blockfrost` is assigned once (`provider.ts`, `initProvider`), by one caller (`initCardano`), called once at boot. No reset exists, and `cardanoReady` goes true only after it. A client exists whenever a real submit can run.
- `submitTransaction` throws with no client, and `submitAnchor` throws unless ready and with a wallet.
- With no credentials, or a key and no mnemonic: not ready. The submitter is not reached and the reconciler is off.
- `DEMO_MODE=true` (compose `ANCHORING_DEMO_MODE`, default false; the process exits under `NODE_ENV=production`) is the ONE configuration where the submitter runs with no client. Its mock hash is 64-hex and passes the real-transaction test, so the ticket's "without a real 64-hex hash" is not the barrier. Its submit is the mock: no fee, and it never throws, so guard 3 cannot fire there. In that mode this PR changes one log line, guard 1's "timed out" to "never reached the chain".

## The design, as Wednesday ruled it (ANSWER 2026-11-06T05:16:22Z)

1. `getTransaction` returns `undefined` with no client and `null` on a 404. A comment at both ends says why, and that the difference is load-bearing.
2. The poller tests strictly for `undefined`. `polled` still moves because the reconciler reads it, `noClient` moves, `lastAnswered*` do not. `noClient` is on the result only when above 0, so a configured client's result has exactly today's keys.
3. `definitelyAbsent` and the log's `answered` use polled minus `noClient`. The rule has two readers, `reconfirmKnownSubmission` and `pollMember` (the family re-poll guard 3 takes when another member exists), and both take it through the predicate.
4. In a mixed window a no-client attempt counts toward NEITHER condition, the same class as a thrown attempt, and the real answers decide. It does not void the window.

Before the first product line I searched, as ruling 5 asks: 0 cells pin `null` for no client, and 0 read a poll result's exact keys (controls: `polled` 12 hits and `toEqual` 1 hit in `ks726-gate-f1`; `evidence/design/ruling5_search.txt`).

**Ruling 6, a configured client whose `txs` resolves undefined:** it reads as no client and rests, the safe direction (cell 8k-9). By read it cannot happen: `txs` returns got's parsed body, and got 11.8.6 under `responseType: 'json'` gives `''` for an empty body or the parsed JSON, never `undefined`. An empty 200 is `''`, which is not `undefined`, so it still counts as an answer, as it does today. No cell pins that.

## Notes for the gate

1. `null` versus `undefined` is a quiet signal. A future bare `vi.fn()` double reads as no client, which fails toward resting; the cheat-sheet fragment says so.
2. With `lastAnswered*` unmoved, a whole no-client window also fails the time condition. So the count's own line reddens only on a mixed window, and the tamper table says which cells catch it.
3. The result's `error` text keeps today's wording, "(N answered, M failed)", which counts a no-client attempt as answered. It has 0 readers in `services/anchoring` by grep.
4. **A defect of mine, found and fixed before this PR.** Two commits: the change, `95f30276872a`, and `17c453253d68`, one test-config line. My first trial merge read 854 of 856: `RED 8k-1` went red by timeout, 8,119 ms against vitest's default 5,000 ms, against 258 ms on an idle run. Each cell loads its modules fresh and that load counts against the limit, and my file set none while the sibling cells set `60_000`. A second run at the fix took 8.7 s and passed, so the slow load recurs on a cold build under load. The two fragments are unchanged by that commit: they state no limit and their figures still hold.
5. The cost the 09-25 ruling named: a transaction that really is absent rests instead of retrying in about 15 s, here only with no client. The one configuration that reaches the submitter with no client cannot reach guard 3, so, by a read of the routes and with no box or table read, no row is affected today.

## Test Evidence

**Touched:** `services/anchoring/src/cardano/provider.ts`, `services/anchoring/src/cardano/confirmation.ts`, `services/anchoring/src/anchorSubmission.ts`; `services/anchoring/src/__tests__/ks1171-8k-no-client-is-not-an-answer.test.ts` (new, 28 cells); a fragment pair under `Projects Documents/fragments/`.

## BLUF for Kam

- **Your ruling:** card `secuura-ks2063-add-session-end-on-role-change-1106` = a, "Both", 2026-11-06T21:04:39+11:00. This is the session-end half. The live-row half is KS 2063.
- **Your second ruling, on gate 245's F1:** card `secuura-ks2083-session-end-race-in-flight-1107` = a, "Merge with the wording corrected, and ticket the race High", 2026-11-08T20:32:11+11:00. Round 2 below is that wording correction and nothing else.
- **What it does:** when an admin changes someone's role, that person's sessions end at once. Before, the old token kept the old role on every route until it expired.
- **Why it matters:** for a request sent after the role change, it closes the walk-around. A demoted `ORG_ADMIN`'s old token could raise a second account, which then passed your live-row check; that request now gets 401. It does not close it for a request already in flight while the sessions end: that request can bring the session back (gate 245 F1, below). That race is on develop for every revoke, and is to be ticketed High by a board seat (your second card).
- **The cost you accepted:** anyone whose role changes, promotions included, is logged out and logs in again.
- **Deploy owed, Kintsugi only:** `auth`. Demo is frozen.

## Round 2: wording only, head `32aa0d06bc0a`

Gate 245 gave round 1 (`d2245bf37fe0`) GO WITH NOTES and said "closes the walk-around" must be corrected. Kam ruled the wording corrected (second card above). This round changes the two KS-2083 fragments and this text. No product or test line changed.

```
git diff --stat d2245bf37fe0..32aa0d06bc0a
 .../fragments/cheat/KS-2083-a-role-change-ends-the-sessions.html      | 4 ++--
 .../fragments/flow/KS-2083-a-role-change-ends-the-sessions.html       | 4 ++--
 2 files changed, 4 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
```

- **Flow fragment:** "closes the walk-around" now holds for a request sent after the change, and names the in-flight race. "Does not close" gains the race, the silent 200 when the store drops after `authenticate()`, and re-sending the held role. The fail-closed line is now the gate's measurement, not a read.
- **Cheat fragment:** the same, shorter, so the pair agrees.
- **Docs check:** `node Blockchain/Dev/scripts/docs-fragments.mjs check` at this head: rc 0, ends OK. A typed section number planted in a scratch copy of the flow fragment: rc 1, FAIL, the fragment named. Its two ADVISORY lines about the committed pages are the same ones round 1's run printed.
- **Merge-tree against develop `a65ae7ed1d60`:** rc 0, clean. The trial tree differs from develop in exactly this PR's 4 files.
- **Push:** through the queue by the existing-branch driver, a plain fast-forward from `d2245bf37fe0`, verified at origin. The pre-push hook printed nothing: by its own header it skips docs-only pushes, so this round has no PREFLIGHT line.
- **Not re-run, because no code or test byte changed:** the auth suite, the new cells, the red proof and the tampers. Round 1's figures below are for `d2245bf37fe0`, whose code this head carries unchanged.
- **Also corrected in this text:** the two-failures paragraph and the KS 1155 sentence (gate 245 F5).

## Gate 254 notes (the compare of round 2: GO WITH NOTES), recorded here, not a new round

- `session.ts:286`, cited for the race in this text and in the flow fragment, is the line of `updateSessionActivity` itself, not of its read or of its write.
- "To be ticketed High" carries no ticket key: no such ticket existed when this was posted (read at 2026-11-08T10:08Z).
- The flow fragment, which ships in the docs, names "Gate 245".

A head is never moved to fix a gate note, so these stay as written.

## What changed

One condition at `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts`, in `PATCH /admin/:id`:

```ts
const roleChanged = safeUpdates.role !== undefined && safeUpdates.role !== target.role;
if (accountStatusForbidsCredential(updatedUser) || roleChanged) {
```

Both sides are canonical: `safeUpdates.role` is normalised earlier in the handler, and `target.role` comes through `mapDbRole`. So naming the role the row already holds, or an alias of it, is not a change. The log title changes from "Admin status change revoked active sessions" to "Admin user change revoked active sessions", and it gains `roleChanged`.

**Who else writes a role, read:** at runtime only this route demotes anyone. I read all 27 `updateUser`-family call sites and 15 raw `UPDATE users` sites across 636 files. The other role writers are the boot seed and claiming an invited stub, and a stub has no session. `evidence/ks2063/role_writers.txt`.

## What this does not close

- **A request in flight while the sessions end can bring the session back** (gate 245 F1, measured on a stand-in store with the real session code, not on real Redis). `updateSessionActivity` (`services/auth/src/services/session.ts:286`, reached from `middleware/authenticate.ts:160` on every request) reads the session record and writes it back whole. A revoke (`session.ts:313`) that lands between the two is undone: the write restores `isActive: true` with a fresh 24 h lifetime, and the session is by then out of `user_sessions`, so no later revoke of all the person's sessions finds it. The gate measured the PATCH answering 200 with the session still live, and the old token then raising a second account. The same race is on develop today for every revoke (a status change, logout), so this PR does not widen it. It is to be ticketed High by a board seat, for a later seat to make the activity write unable to resurrect a revoked record (Kam's card `secuura-ks2083-session-end-race-in-flight-1107` = a). So "closes the walk-around" holds for a request sent after the change only.
- **If the session store drops after `authenticate()`, the PATCH answers 200 with nothing revoked** (gate 245 F2). `session.ts:332` returns 0 and `routes/users.ts:846` takes it, logging `sessionsRevoked: 0` at info; the role is written. The gate measured the old session live again once the store heals. KS 1407 fixed this class on the password path; the status path has it too. The card puts the store-down case on the same new ticket.
- **Re-sending the role the row already holds cannot end a stale token** (gate 245 F4). `routes/users.ts:844` compares the new role with the row, not with the token, so someone demoted before this deploys, or by hand, is cut off only by a real role change or a status change.
- **While the gateway cannot reach the session store it forwards anyway,** by design, so a Redis blip does not refuse all traffic. Measured at the gateway: `evidence/ks2063/gateway_rows.txt`.
- **Auth's own `authenticate()` fails closed on a store outage:** 401 with the store flag down, 500 with the store rejecting, the peer unchanged both ways. Round 1 called this a read; gate 245 measured it.
- **A role edited by hand in SQL** ends nothing.
- **A key minted before the demotion stays valid.** Neither this nor KS 2063 retires it.

## Kept and named, not changed

A revoke that throws after the role is written answers 500 with the role already changed. The status path does the same today, and the password paths handle it differently under KS 1407. Changing that is wider than this ticket, as Wednesday ruled (ANSWER 2026-11-06T10:08:50Z). Two cells pin it, one for each path.

## Test Evidence

**Touched:** 4 files. Product 1: `routes/users.ts`. New test 1. Docs 2: the fragment pair. No inventory edit: that doc makes no claim about sessions on a role change.

**Ran, Node v26.8.1, not an LTS line, on the Mac host:**

| What | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New cells at develop | RED 11 of 11 by assertion, controls 18 of 18 |

**The two that did not pass in the whole suite,** both `ks949`'s walk of the tree, ran past their 5 s budget: 5,004 and 5,003 ms in the full run, vitest timeouts (`STACK_TRACE_ERROR`), not assertions. Alone, in this new clone, the first run read 29 of 31: the walk cell timed out at 5,001 ms, and the cell "is NOT seeded when DEMO_SECUURA_PASSWORD is unset" at 7,047 ms, a cold import of the user repository, not a walk (round 1 hung the 7,047 ms on the walk; gate 245 F5). The next two runs read 31 of 31, slowest cell 1,293 ms and 410 ms. Gate 245 found the cause: a first read of a cold DevMASTER tree, 17,633 to 24,851 ms for the first walk against vitest's 5 s default, 102 to 143 ms on later walks; the same two cells fail at develop. KS 1155's title is about the `packages/shared` tree-walking guards; its comments of 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-27 record `ks949` as the same class in `services/auth`, and its description points at KS 1053 for that cell. No other cell failed.

**Bytes since those runs:** the ticket key replaced a placeholder in one code comment and in the test's header, and the test file was renamed. No logic changed. At this head I re-ran the new cells, 29 of 29, the ratchet and the docs check. The red proof, the tampers and the whole-suite run are from just before the rename.

**Hook, verbatim:** PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.

**NOT run:** the four platform suites; a local stack; a real login or decoded token; real Redis; any box; a Node LTS line.

**NOT covered:**

What changes, in `services/mcp-server/src/http-server.ts`:
- `POST /hash`, `POST /verify` and, per item, `POST /register-batch` and `POST /verify-batch` no longer read a caller-supplied `filePath`. A truthy `filePath` of any type is refused with one fixed sentence, `filePath is not accepted by this interface; the server reads no path`: HTTP 400 on `/hash` and `/verify`, a failed item inside the batch's 200. **Behaviour change to read:** the refusal also applies when `content`, `documentId` or `contentHash` is sent beside `filePath` (the field was ignored then). A falsy `filePath` (empty string, null, 0, false) passes as before. The module reads no file: `hashing.ts` is imported for `hashBuffer` only, and a structural cell scans the import specifiers.
- The two 400 texts that named the option drop it: `Provide base64-encoded content` and `Provide documentId or contentHash`.
- The `POST /hash` 500 logs the error's message with `console.error` and answers the constant `An unexpected error occurred`; it used to echo the thrown text, a file-system error naming the path.
- **New in round 2: a parser or router error answers the constant too.** Malformed JSON, a body over 1 MB, an unsupported charset and an undecodable path parameter never reach a route handler, so none of the catch blocks saw them, and Express's default handler answered an HTML page with the error text and a stack naming server file paths whenever `NODE_ENV` is not `production` (the compose file sets `development`; a generated customer package sets nothing). One error middleware after the routes now answers `{success:false, error:{code, message:"An unexpected error occurred"}}`, keeps the 4xx status (400 `BAD_REQUEST`, 413 `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, 415 `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`, anything else 4xx `BAD_REQUEST`, otherwise 500), and logs the error's name, type and status only, never its message (a malformed `/generate-package` body could hold part of an apiKey).
- The `content` branch of `POST /hash` is unchanged.
- Spec and guides: `services/mcp-server/openapi.yaml` and its byte copy `MCP Deployment/openapi.yaml` (pinned byte-identical by a cell) no longer describe `filePath`, describe the refusal on all four routes, and document the 400 and 413 answers of `/hash` and `/verify`, `VerificationResult.error` and the 1 MB limit; `Blockchain/Dev/services/mcp-server/src/mcp-server.openapi.ts`, the zod spec source (imported by nothing), has the refusal on `/hash` and `/verify` only, with no 413, no 1 MB limit and no batch refusal outside a comment. Only the generic HTTP agent guide, `Blockchain/Dev/MCP Deployment/generic-http-agent.md`, states the 1 MB limit.
- The stdio MCP tools (`src/tools/*`) are a different surface and are not changed.

**Gate 239 findings fixed in this head:** F1 the guides stop sending a file as base64 in `-d` and hash locally; F2 the parser/router error handler above, with a new real-server test file; F3 the refusal sentence is now `filePath is not accepted by this interface; the server reads no path`; F4 the stale guide line; F5 the spec describes the refusal on all four routes with the 400 and 413 answers; F6 a structural no-file-system cell, non-string truthy `filePath` values, and `0`/`false` pinned as falsy; F7 test headers reworded and `EXEMPT` renamed `HASH_ROUTE`.

With `NODE_ENV=production`, `enforceProductionConfig` exits 1 when a service holds one of the values `env.example` publishes (exact match after trim; the message names the variable, never the value). Measured on the production render: every service that receives one of these names already calls `enforceProductionConfig`, so no service `index.ts` is touched.

  - Not in the table, on purpose: `DEMO_SERVICE_KEY` (demo-service does not use the shared guard and is out of the default render), `APP_DB_PASSWORD` (gate 233: neutral; compose falls back to a literal; KS-762). `VITE_CARDANO_NETWORK` has no boot guard (static frontend); the overlay derives it from `CARDANO_NETWORK`, which three backend services refuse while it holds `preview`.

## Linear

**No ticket.** This is the session-end `5_Project_History/history.md` update the platform-k `CLAUDE.md` checklist requires; it records local-only diagnosis and carries no product change. The nearest related tickets are referenced in the entry itself — KS-380 (preflight), KS-469 (host install drift), KS-666 (stack guard / slots), KS-949 (seed idempotence test) — but none owns this housekeeping. The `Linear ticket present` check will warn; that is the intended reading.

## Summary

Adds the **21 September 2026** entry to `5_Project_History/history.md` (+18 lines, top of the file, house style). It records:

- **Two `--rebuild` runs OOM-killed the frontend `vite build`s** (`SIGKILL … cannot allocate memory`) — root cause is the environment, not the tree: a 7.65 GiB Docker Desktop VM on a 32 GB Mac with 109 containers (3 Secuura stacks + 2 SSD stacks, ~4.5 GiB) leaving the `mybuilder` buildkit container too little for `issuer-frontend` (3,966 modules + terser).
- **Recovery:** slot 2 stopped with volumes kept (slot 3 and the SSD stacks were found already down beforehand — volumes intact); `issuer-frontend` rebuilt alone in 34 s; slot 1 brought up **33/33 healthy** with gateway `/health`, the three portals and the demo login all 200.
- `npm ci` in `Blockchain/Dev` clearing the KS-469 "host install BEHIND lockfile" warning.
- **KS-380 preflight 14/15 → 15/15**: leg 14 failed only on `ks949_main_seed_idempotence` because the host shell had no locale (Homebrew postgres: *postmaster became multithreaded during startup*); passes 27/27 and the full sweep passes 15/15 with `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8`, now exported from the author's `~/.bash_profile`.
- Two open follow-ups noted, neither actioned: raise Docker Desktop memory 8 → 16 GB; slot 3 / SSD stacks left down.

Nothing was deployed; the VM demo is untouched.

## Test Evidence

- **touched:** `5_Project_History/history.md` only
- **ran:** `git diff --stat` (1 file, +18/−0); grep of the added text for external-org `github.com` links per the KS-1270/1271 rule — 0 found. On the same `develop` head (`7be81d5c9`) this session also ran the full KS-380 preflight against the live slot-1 stack: **PASSED — 15/15 legs** (shell suites 41/41, 13 code guards, 100 KS-666 invariants, spec-drift/lockfile/spec-auth/path-resolvability/npm-audit/standalone-lock gates) — that is evidence about the tree the entry describes, not about this diff.
- **NOT run:** Schemathesis, Akto, Playwright, k6, service unit suites — no code changed.
- **migrations + config:** none.

## Test plan

- [x] Rendered Markdown reads correctly at the top of `5_Project_History/history.md` (newest-first ordering preserved, closing `---` present)
- [x] No external-organisation GitHub cross-references in the added text

## KS-961 — the aggregate workspace suite has never run on a PR

Kam ruled **`wire-nonblocking`** (2026-09-07 11:41): wire it advisory first, decide on blocking from the evidence.

### The gap
`npm run test --workspaces --if-present` exists in exactly two workflows — `ci.yml:51` (`workflow_dispatch` **only**) and `deploy-demo.yml:140` (**after merge**, at deploy). So merged code is the first code the aggregate suite sees.

### ⚠ The job cannot run today, and the comment in it says so
Actions is retired for this repo. Measured via the Actions API 2026-09-07: **the twenty most recent runs are all run-level `startup_failure` with zero jobs**, including runs triggered minutes earlier by a push. **A workflow configured to run on `pull_request` is not evidence that it runs** — that reading is what made this gap look smaller than it is.

So this PR ships **two** things: the job (correct for when Actions returns, and mirroring the `migrations` job above it which already carries the same disclosure), and a **`docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` row under Manual CI-gate equivalents** with the local command and its baseline — the gate that actually operates.

### 🔴 The measured baseline decides the blocking question

Run on develop `61df129e9`:

| | |
|---|---|
| wall-clock | **32 s** |
| workspaces with a `test` script | **26** |
| skipped **silently** by `--if-present` | **6** (all of `frontend/`) |
| exit code | **1** |
| failing workspaces | **2** — `@secuura/anchoring-service` 1/172 (`threadTokenMint`), `@secuura/originate` 2/480 (`ks444` webhooks) |

**Both failures are pre-existing on develop**, verified by running each workspace on develop with no branch changes in the tree.

**The aggregate lane is RED today.** Wired blocking, it would have blocked every PR in the repo from the moment it landed — including Peter's and Stuart's. Advisory-first was the right call; making it blocking needs those two suites green.

### Test Evidence
**Head `3aee3deed` (2026-09-14) = `cb7a3e3be` (the head Peter reviewed) + one `--no-ff` merge of develop `8861e6216` (clean; `de376a9f1`) + one doc-only commit `3aee3deed`. The workflow file is byte-identical to the reviewed head — no workflow line changed after Peter's read.**

**Touched:** `.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml` (+1 advisory job — unchanged since `cb7a3e3be`), `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` (+1 section; **this round:** the baseline table gains a second dated column measured at this head, Peter's 2026-09-07 column kept as history, and the "it cannot run today" sentence becomes a dated statement — Actions resumed 2026-09-09 — with the rule that the manual row still operates).

**Ran (the re-run Peter asked for in review `5153400898`, posted on the PR as a comment):** `npm ci` → `npm run build --workspaces --if-present` → `npm run test --workspaces --if-present` in `Blockchain/Dev`, twice in a fresh tree — at `cb7a3e3be`: **40 s · 26 workspaces · 6 skipped · exit 1 · 2 failing** (`anchoring-service` 1/172 `threadTokenMint`; `originate` 2/515 `ks444` webhooks) — and at the merged tree: **58 s · 26 · 6 · exit 1 · 1 failing** (`anchoring-service` 1/208 `threadTokenMint`; `originate` 0/588 — the two `ks444` cells are green on develop). `openssl version` = OpenSSL 3.6.3 (Homebrew first on `PATH`); `auth-service` 635/635 both runs. Each failing workspace's own tally line is in the PR comment. **The push preflight RAN on this push (the doc is a `Blockchain/Dev` path): `PREFLIGHT PASSED.` with **11 of 14 legs run** — legs 3/4/8 SKIP (gateway closed by HOLD: `GATEWAY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9`), leg 5 `59 audit-contract cases pass`, legs 6/7 `no advisories outside the triaged baseline` (baseline blob `03d1680e3` = develop's), leg 12 `all 29 tracked shell suite(s) are reached`, leg 14 `shell suites: 29 passed, 0 failed (of 29)` in 232 s.**

**Ran — the job itself, for the first time anywhere:** `pr` run 34786655660 at this head, job `Workspace unit suites (advisory, non-blocking)` 103803259738 — counts step `26` / `6` printed; `npm ci` green; **build step FAILED on the Linux runner** — `demo-overlay` and `outlook-addin` (the two vite-6 frontends) die on a missing rollup Linux binary because `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` records only the macOS one (`rollup-darwin-arm64`; npm/cli#4828) — so **step 7, the suites, was SKIPPED and no suite executed on GitHub**; the four vite-8 frontends and all 26 service/package builds were green. Advisory, blocks nothing; the lockfile matter is outside this PR (raised for filing). Node on the runner: v26.8.2 (`node-version: current`). (the 2026-09-07 "NOT run: it cannot run" line below is superseded by this; kept as the record of what was true when written).

**NOT run:** the four platform suites (CI config + docs; no runtime code); a gateway-UP preflight (no stack was started; legs 3/4/8 of the preflight skipped by that, ratio stated above); the job's `:118-124` comment block still says "IT CANNOT RUN TODAY" — stale, deliberately not edited (a workflow edit beyond this PR's reviewed diff is held for the merge decision).

**Migrations + config:** none. No service, route, schema or migration touched.

### Notes
`--if-present` skips six workspaces without a word, so a green run does not say how many suites executed — the job prints the counts *before* running. No `|| true` and no exit-code laundering: the job-level `continue-on-error` is what makes it advisory, keeping the step's real result in the log rather than rewriting it to success.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Changelog

Sourced from @​radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu's changelog.

2.1.24

  • Reverted breaking changes that caused compatibility issues with React Server Components.
  • Updated dependencies: @radix-ui/react-compose-refs@1.1.5, @radix-ui/react-context@1.2.2, @radix-ui/react-id@1.1.4, @radix-ui/react-menu@2.1.24, @radix-ui/react-primitive@2.1.10, @radix-ui/react-use-controllable-state@1.2.6

2.1.23

  • Updated dependencies: @radix-ui/react-menu@2.1.23, @radix-ui/react-primitive@2.1.9

2.1.22

  • Republish through CI to attach provenance attestations. The previous versions of these packages were published manually outside of CI and therefore shipped without provenance; this patch re-releases the same code through the CI pipeline so every package includes an attestation.
  • Updated dependencies: @radix-ui/primitive@1.1.7, @radix-ui/react-compose-refs@1.1.4, @radix-ui/react-context@1.2.1, @radix-ui/react-id@1.1.3, @radix-ui/react-menu@2.1.22, @radix-ui/react-primitive@2.1.8, @radix-ui/react-use-controllable-state@1.2.5

2.1.21

  • Improved tree-shaking so bundlers can drop unused components. Component parts are now marked /* @__PURE__ */ and use named render functions instead of Component.displayName = ... assignments, which previously prevented dead-code elimination with some bundlers.
  • Updated dependencies: @radix-ui/react-menu@2.1.21, @radix-ui/react-use-controllable-state@1.2.4, @radix-ui/primitive@1.1.6, @radix-ui/react-compose-refs@1.1.3, @radix-ui/react-context@1.2.0, @radix-ui/react-id@1.1.2, @radix-ui/react-primitive@2.1.7

2.1.20

  • Fixed menu items, tab triggers, toolbar links, and select items intercepting Space/Enter keys that originate from focusable descendants.
  • Updated dependencies: @radix-ui/primitive@1.1.5, @radix-ui/react-context@1.2.0, @radix-ui/react-menu@2.1.20

2.1.19

  • Fixed infinite re-render loop in React 19 caused by unstable composed ref callback references.

Other updates

  • Updated dependencies: @radix-ui/react-primitive@2.1.7, @radix-ui/react-menu@2.1.19

2.1.18

  • Fixed a bug where menus and submenus remained open after a window loses focus.
  • Updated dependencies: @radix-ui/react-menu@2.1.18, @radix-ui/react-primitive@2.1.6

2.1.17

  • Added repository.directory to all package.json files
  • Updated dependencies: @radix-ui/react-menu@2.1.17, @radix-ui/primitive@1.1.4, @radix-ui/react-compose-refs@1.1.3, @radix-ui/react-context@1.1.4, @radix-ui/react-id@1.1.2, @radix-ui/react-primitive@2.1.5, @radix-ui/react-use-controllable-state@1.2.3
